Borrowing is fine for one light load, but check the owner's insurance covers other drivers before you fill it.

Hiss with nothing plugged in is normal for a valve amp, and a buzz that stops when you touch the strings or turn down the guitar's volume is the room's wiring or a single-coil pickup, not a fault: stand further from the amp, turn your body, and keep a phone and a dimmer switch away from it. If it hums with a cable in and nothing else, swap the cable; if it crackles when you move the guitar lead, the jack is loose; if it buzzes only on one socket in the house, try another room before you blame the amp.

Hoarding is a recognised condition, and it is treatable: CBT from a therapist who works on hoarding is what helps, so the first step is a GP appointment, and it is worth saying how much of the home is unusable and whether anyone is at risk. Don't let anyone clear the house for you in one go — it usually comes back and it is frightening to lose things that way. Start with one shelf or one drawer, decide on the smallest thing first, and ask the GP about a referral to the local hoarding or mental health team. Mind and Hoarding UK both advise families too, and Hoarding UK runs support groups.

Hold the phone at eye level and a little above, just past arm's length, and turn your face towards a window or a lamp rather than towards the screen: light on the front of the face is the whole difference. Tap your face on the screen first, so the camera sets the brightness for your skin and not for the sky behind you, and take three or four - one will have your eyes open. Wipe the lens on your sleeve before you start.

Hold the power button for ten seconds to force it off, wait a few seconds and start it again; you lose unsaved work but nothing else. If it happens often, check free disk space and start it without the extras (Safe Mode) to see whether an update or a startup app is the cause.

Hold the side button and the volume button together until Slide to power off appears on an iPhone; on Android hold the power button and tap Power off. A phone that will not respond needs a forced restart instead: press volume up, volume down, then hold the side button until the logo shows.

Hold the clock button until the hour flashes, turn or press the plus and minus to the right hour, press clock again for the minutes, then press it once more to save - the symbol on most ovens is a small clock or a bell. On a touch panel the same steps are under Settings or the clock icon, and if the display will not go into flashing it is usually still showing a timer: press the timer button to clear it first. After a power cut most ovens come back flashing 12:00 and need the same steps.

Hold the knife in a pinch grip - thumb and forefinger pinching the blade where it meets the handle, the other three fingers round the handle - which lines the blade up with your forearm and gives you control. On the other hand, curl the fingertips under so the knuckles lead and the flat of the blade rides against them, because that is what keeps fingers clear rather than watching them. Keep the tip down on the board and push forward instead of chopping up and down, and keep the knife sharp: a blunt one skids off onion skin and that is when people cut themselves.

Hold the knob in for twenty seconds after the flame catches, then let it go: a pilot that won't hold is nearly always the thermocouple, a small part a Gas Safe engineer swaps in ten minutes. A draught or a dirty jet does it too, and both mean taking the case off, so that is their job as well. If you smell gas, turn it off at the meter, open the windows and ring the gas emergency line on 0800 111 999.

Hold the letter down and pick the accented one from the pop-up on a Mac, an iPhone or Android. On Windows, press Windows and full stop for the symbol panel and choose it there, or hold Alt and type 0233 on the number pad for e-acute. If you need them often, add the United States-International layout (Settings > Time & language > Language): then an apostrophe and e gives e-acute, and a tilde and n gives n-tilde. A Mac calls the same layout ABC - Extended.

Hold two corners of the same short end and tuck one inside the other so the elastic sits together, then let the whole sheet hang and give it a shake: it falls into a rough half. Lay it flat, tuck the two loose elastic corners into the same pocket, then fold the long side in thirds so the elastic is hidden inside, and fold the bundle in half. It will not be a perfect rectangle, and it does not need to be - what makes a sheet easy to store is that it is flat and the elastic is not on the outside.

Hold a warm, clean flannel against it for ten minutes, three or four times a day: that helps it drain, usually within two weeks. Don't squeeze it, and leave off eye make-up and contact lenses until it has gone. A hard, painless lump on the lid is a chalazion and wants the same warmth. See a pharmacist or GP if it has not settled in a week, or the lid is red and swollen.

Hold it between the thumb and the side of the curled index finger, with just a few millimetres showing, and grip it as lightly as you can without it turning - most beginners squeeze and the pick fights back. A thin pick (0.5 to 0.6mm) is easier for strumming chords, a thicker one (1mm) for single notes, and if it keeps slipping, the ones with a textured or drilled grip are worth the extra pound. Strum from the wrist with the arm still, and let the pick pass across the strings at a slight angle rather than flat, which is what stops the catching and the dropping.

Hold it in the fingers of your left hand, not the palm, with the handle running from the base of the little finger to the knuckle of the index finger, then lay the right hand over the top so both Vs point at your right shoulder. Squeeze about three out of ten: a tight grip stops the wrists hinging, which is where the distance comes from.

Homemade custard keeps 2 days in the fridge, in a jug with a lid or a sheet of cling film pressed onto the surface so no skin forms. Reheat it gently and stir rather than boiling it, and bin any that has stood on the table through dinner.

Homophones sound the same but are spelt differently and mean different things: their/there/they're, to/too/two, right/write, sea/see. If swapping a word changes the sentence's meaning, you have a homophone pair - that is what the other half of these questions is about.

Honey does not really go off - a jar keeps for years: honey that clouds or sets hard has crystallised rather than spoiled, and both are normal. Stand the jar in a bowl of hot water to loosen it, and keep it in a cupboard with the lid on. The one rule is no honey for a baby under a year, because of the botulism risk.

Hook the bras, put them in a mesh laundry bag, and wash on a delicates cycle at 30C with a liquid detergent; never a hot wash or the dryer, which wrecks the elastic. Silk and anything lacy is safer hand-washed in cool water with a little shampoo.

Hot water opens up the blood vessels near the skin, so blood pressure drops and standing up quickly leaves you light-headed - it is common, and it is not a sign of anything wrong in a healthy person. Get out slowly, sit down on the edge for a minute, keep the water warm rather than hot, drink some water and eat beforehand. If you actually faint, or it happens every time, or it comes with chest pain or palpitations, get it checked.

Hot water that runs hot and then cold is the tank running out, not overheating: cold water comes in at the bottom and pushes the hot out of the top, so the last of it comes through cool. Set the cylinder thermostat to 60-65 degrees, which is also the temperature that keeps bacteria down, and see whether a second long shower is what empties it. With two elements, the bottom one having gone is why a tank heats for a minute and then gives up. A combi has no tank, so hot-then-cold there is the diverter valve or somebody else's tap.

Hot water and a soft brush while it is still warm, no washing-up liquid and never a soak, then dry it on the hob over a low heat and wipe a smear of oil round the inside with kitchen paper. That thin film is the whole of the care. If a patch of rust appears, scour just that spot, dry it, and season it again on the heat - a wok is not non-stick, it gets closer every time you cook in it.

Hot water from the boiler flows through the radiator, warms the metal, and the air next to it warms, rises and pulls cooler air in across the floor. Most of the heat reaches the room that way rather than by the panel glowing, which is why a shelf above one or a sofa in front of one wastes it.

Hot at the top and cold at the bottom is sludge sitting in the radiator, not air, so bleeding it will not help: the water cannot get round the bottom. Ask a heating engineer to power-flush the system or add a chemical cleaner, and have a magnetic filter fitted so it does not come back. Turning the other radiators off to push water through the cold one is a five-minute test that shows whether it is sludge or a stuck valve.

Hot flushes before 40 are usually not the menopause: an overactive thyroid is the commonest cause, and an infection, some medicines and low oestrogen from another cause do it too. The GP's first check is a thyroid blood test - and a pregnancy test before anything else if your periods have stopped. Note down how often they come and whether they bring a racing heart or weight change, because that is what tells the causes apart. See a GP if they are frequent, and the same day if you also have a fever or feel faint.

Hot flushes in midlife - most often the late forties and fifties - are usually perimenopause: keep the room cool, wear thin layers, cut back on alcohol and caffeine, and use a fan at night. HRT is the most effective treatment and is safe for most women - talk to a GP about your own risks, and mention any flushes with weight loss, a lump or bleeding after sex.

Household rubbish is free at a council tip; what they charge for is the DIY waste - rubble, soil, plasterboard, old tyres and sometimes garden waste - and the price is set by your council, so check its page for your site before you load the car. Vans and trailers usually need a permit booked in advance, and a few sites want proof you live in the area.
How ready do you feel for it?

How you feel changes first: two to three weeks of regular sessions and the stairs and your sleep are easier. Visible change takes about six to eight weeks, and the real difference by three to six months when it shows in what you can do rather than in the mirror. Three sessions a week that you actually keep beat five you abandon.

How long it takes comes from how big the job is and how fast it goes, so the number to find is the rate rather than the total, and the rate is published - on the pack, in the recipe, or by whoever does the work. Tell me the two figures and I will work out the time.

However long your contract says - three to six months is usual - probation is a check that you turn up and learn, so do the plain things well: on time, ask early when unsure, and flag anything that slips before it slips. Ask your manager in week four what would make it a clear yes, then do exactly that. The notice during probation is usually shorter than after it, and it is in your contract; an extension should come with a reason and a date, so ask for both in writing. If it ends, ask why in an email - a no for a reason you can fix is worth more than a shrug.

Hummus keeps about a week in the fridge in a sealed tub, and 3 to 4 days once a spoon has been in it: the date on the lid is for the sealed pot, so a couple of days past it is usually fine. A film of water on top is normal, so stir it in. Bin it if it smells sour or fizzy, or if there is mould.

Hummus keeps about a week in the fridge in a sealed tub, and it freezes well for about four months. To freeze it, smooth it flat in a tub, thaw it overnight in the fridge and stir it well, adding a squeeze of lemon and a splash of water when it comes back, since it returns a little grainy. Leave off the pool of oil and the swirl until you serve it, because they separate.

Hunger on its own gives you a rumbling stomach and a dip in mood; a hypo also brings the shakes, sweat, a fast heart and tingling lips, and it comes on fast. If you have diabetes and cannot test, treat it as a hypo - 15g of fast sugar settles hunger too and costs you little. If it keeps happening an hour or two after meals, the dose or the meal is worth looking at rather than eating more.
I'd be there if I could. I'm not, so let me help from here: how many are coming, and what have you got left to sort?

IBS stands for irritable bowel syndrome: cramping, bloating, wind and a change in how often you go, with nothing wrong with the gut itself. It is managed rather than cured - regular meals, enough fibre and water, less caffeine and alcohol - and a GP can rule out coeliac disease and check a change you have never had before.

IBS is a gut that is sensitive rather than damaged: cramping, bloating, wind and a bowel that swings between loose and constipated, often for years, with nothing wrong found on tests. It is managed rather than cured. Eat at regular times, keep to soluble fibre - oats, psyllium, peeled fruit - rather than a lot of bran, drink peppermint tea for the cramps, and try a probiotic for a month; a dietitian-led low-FODMAP diet is the next step and is not one to guess at. See a GP for the diagnosis, and go sooner for blood in the stool, weight loss, a lump, or waking at night with pain, which are not IBS.

ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

ISA stands for individual savings account: a wrapper rather than a product, so a cash ISA and a stocks-and-shares ISA are both ISAs and what is inside them is free of UK tax on interest and gains. The allowance is per person, per tax year, and it resets in April whether or not you used the last one.

IUD stands for intrauterine device: the small T-shaped coil a doctor or nurse fits into the womb, and it lasts five to ten years - a copper one five, the hormonal ones three to eight. Fitting takes a few minutes at a clinic or GP surgery, it is free on the NHS, and cramping for a day or two afterwards is usual. A copper one also works as emergency contraception up to five days after sex, the hormonal ones usually make periods lighter or stop them, and as long as you are over 16 you can ask for one without telling anyone.

IVF stands for in vitro fertilisation: an egg is fertilised with sperm in a laboratory, and an embryo is put back into the womb. One cycle takes about four to six weeks, the NHS funds a set number depending on where you live and your age, and the chance of success falls steeply through the late thirties.

Ibuprofen suits pain with swelling or inflammation - a sprain, period pain, toothache - taken with food. Paracetamol suits a plain headache or a temperature, and it is the one to use if ibuprofen upsets your stomach, you are pregnant, or you take a blood thinner. If one alone is not enough they can be taken together, on their own schedules.

Ibuprofen and the other anti-inflammatories push blood pressure up a little and blunt the tablets that are meant to bring it down, so paracetamol is the painkiller to use if you take one every day. A single dose for a headache is not the problem; a week of them is. Ask a pharmacist if you need an anti-inflammatory for more than a few days.

Ibuprofen and the other anti-inflammatories make the blood a little slower to clot, which is why they are stopped before an operation or a tooth out - usually a few days before, on the surgeon's or dentist's word - and why they are not mixed with warfarin or a blood thinner without advice. Paracetamol has no effect on clotting at all, so if you bruise easily or bleed for longer than you used to, that is a question for a pharmacist or GP rather than a reason to keep taking it.

Ice cubes keep for months in a sealed bag or box, but they pick up freezer smells within a few weeks, and they shrink and go cloudy as the ice slowly turns to vapour. Seal the tray's cubes in a bag, use them within about three months, and bin any that smell of the freezer - ice takes on the smell of whatever is next to it.

Ice in a fridge that is meant to look after itself comes from one of three things: a door seal that no longer grips (shut a strip of paper in the door and pull - it should drag), the drain hole at the back of the fridge blocked so the water freezes there, or food pushed against the back wall. Fix the seal and clear the drain and the ice stops coming back. Get rid of what is there by defrosting it properly with the door open overnight, and never chip at it with a knife.

Icy ice cream is water freezing into crystals: more fat and sugar (cream instead of milk, a spoon of glucose or a splash of alcohol), churn it cold, and stir a home-made tub every 30 minutes for the first 3 hours so the crystals stay small. A freezer that runs very cold makes it harder still, so move it to the door shelf.

Idina Menzel is the voice of Elsa in Frozen (2013) and Frozen 2 (2019) and sings Let It Go; Kristen Bell is Anna. Both films are U certificates of about 100 minutes, so they are fine for a three year old - the ice monster in the first one is the only bit that frightens some small children.

If pain is what wakes you, treat the pain rather than the sleep: take a painkiller half an hour before bed if you can, prop the sore part on a pillow and put a rolled towel under a bad back. Warm bath and gentle stretches before bed loosen a stiff shoulder or hip. If it wakes you most nights for weeks, or comes with numbness, weakness or weight loss, get it looked at.

If the noise is coming from outside your room, earplugs and a heavy curtain take the edge off, and a fan or white noise can mask it. If it is a neighbour and it happens often, your council's noise team can act on it; a short log of the times is what they ask for.

If the organiser cancels the package you are owed a full refund within 14 days, and if they cancel inside 14 days of leaving you can claim compensation on top. The organiser named on the booking owes it, not the hotel: ask in writing, then the card company, which is jointly liable over £100. An ATOL certificate pays for a replacement holiday or your money back when the company goes under.

If the revs rise but the speed doesn't, or the bite point is right at the top of the pedal, the clutch is on its way out; a judder as you pull away is the flywheel or an engine mount. A replacement is usually £300 to £800 depending on the car, and it is cheaper to do before it fails completely. Stop riding the clutch in traffic to make it last.

If the shop cannot supply what you ordered the money comes back in full, and you are not asking a favour: a shop that cancels owes a full refund within 14 days, delivery included, and one that cannot say when stock is back owes it as soon as you cancel. Ask in writing with the order number; if they stall, your card provider can charge the payment back with that email as proof.

If the shower runs cold but the hot taps elsewhere are fine, it is the shower: an electric shower usually wants the pull cord or a tripped switch in the consumer unit checked, and a mixer shower is often a stuck thermostatic cartridge, which frees up if you take the head off and work the temperature knob from cold to hot a few times. If the hot taps are cold too, the fault is the boiler or the cylinder rather than the shower.

If the bill charges more than the shelf price or the menu, ask for the difference back: the price displayed is the price you pay. If they refuse, keep the receipt and a photo of the label or the menu, complain in writing, then use a chargeback or the small claims court.

If the business is transferred as a going concern, your contract usually moves with it on the same terms - that is TUPE in the UK - so your pay, holiday, notice and pension carry over and a change to any of them needs a good reason. Ask the new owner in writing for the transfer letter, who your employer will be on day one, and whether any roles are at risk; keep copies of your contract and your last pay slips. A merger is not a redundancy, and "at risk" has to be said in writing before anything happens.

If the company has paid its bills, filed its accounts and has no debts, the cheap route is a voluntary strike-off: form DS01, signed by the directors, £8 online, and it is gone about two to three months later once Companies House advertises it. Clear the bank account and deal with the assets first - anything left becomes property of the Crown. If there are debts or a bounce-back loan, do not strike it off: a members' voluntary liquidation through an insolvency practitioner is the orderly way, and an accountant will price it.

If they cancel, the deposit comes back and they should find you the same thing elsewhere at their cost: ring, then put it in writing - the booking, the date, what you paid - and ask what they are offering. Keep the confirmation and the messages, because a chargeback on the card needs them. If you are out of pocket on something booked around it, say the figure in the same message.

If you are drinking far more than usual and still thirsty, see a GP: thirst that will not quench is worth a blood test, because it can be the first sign of diabetes. If it is just habit, spread the day's drinks out, keep water out of sight between meals, and sip rather than down a pint at once - but do not ration it, since your body asks for what it needs.

If you cannot pass urine at all and your bladder is full and painful, that needs looking at the same day: ring 111 or go to A&E, because waiting makes it worse and it can back up into the kidneys. If it is a weak dribble rather than nothing, drink water through the day and get a GP appointment, and go the same day if there is a fever or blood.

If you go up more than a few times a year, get one: a folding aluminium loft ladder bolted to the hatch frame is far safer than carrying a step ladder up, and it stows in the opening. Measure the floor-to-ceiling height and the clear size of the hatch first and match the ladder's stated height to it, because a ladder that is too short leaves the last step below the floor. Fit it to a timber surround rather than plasterboard, and only board the loft along the joists - a ceiling is built to hold a ceiling, not a person.

If you know the name, use it: 'Dear Ms Okafor' or 'Dear Dr Patel' beats any general form. 'Dear Sir or Madam' is fine when you genuinely have no name, and it pairs with 'Yours faithfully'; with a name it is 'Yours sincerely'. Never 'To whom it may concern' - it reads like a circular - and check the spelling of the name, which is the thing people notice most.

If HMRC owes you, the letter is a P800 and the money comes back by itself once you confirm your bank details in your online tax account - no agent needed, and anyone who rings you about a rebate is a scam. If you think it is missing, claim with form P87 online for work expenses (up to four years back), and for a flat-rate homeworker claim it is £6 a week. Give it eight weeks before chasing.

If a child is shut in, ring 999 straight away and stay on the line. Otherwise get a window open and shout to a neighbour, or ring someone who has a spare key - someone is nearly always in. If nobody is, the landlord or letting agent first, then a locksmith who quotes on the phone; a stuck lock is worth one firm push with the handle held up before you pay anyone. If there is fire, smoke or someone unwell, ring 999 and say you are locked in.

If a fingernail doesn't catch on it, the scratch is in the lacquer: clean it, polish with a cutting compound, then wax, and it will mostly vanish. If your nail catches, a paint pen for £10 to £20 stops the rust and makes it much less obvious, and only a bodyshop will make it perfect.

If it rings or buzzes but the screen stays black, the phone is alive and the fault is the display or its backlight, so force a restart rather than charging it: on an iPhone press volume up, volume down, then hold the side button until the Apple logo shows; on Android hold power and volume down for ten to fifteen seconds. If it comes back, back it up straight away, because a display that has gone once usually goes again. If it stays black and it still rings, it is the screen or its connector - a repair shop job, and ask them to test it before you agree a price.

If it smells sour, or wrong rather than just strong, bin it - cooking does not make an off food safe. Cooked rice, cooked meat and anything with a sauce are the strict ones; hard cheese and dry bread are the ones you can judge by looking.

If it had raisins, currants or sultanas in it, ring your vet today and say how much went down: a Christmas pudding or a spotted dick can shut down a dog's kidneys, and no amount is known to be safe. A plain rice, Yorkshire or black pudding has none of those, so it is not poison, but it is rich - a taste only, and ring the vet if the dog is sick or dribbling.

If it has come up red, swollen and throbbing, especially with pus at the side or base of the nail, that is a bacterial infection of the nail fold (paronychia) and it is not the slow yellow fungus: soak it in warm salty water, don't squeeze it, and see a pharmacist or GP quickly because it often needs an antibiotic. A nail that is thick, yellow or crumbly, and has been for months, is the fungal one - that takes a lacquer or tablets and months while the nail grows out.

If it is not tax, national insurance, a court order or something you signed up to in writing, taking money off your pay is unlawful: a till shortfall, a breakage or a fine for being late usually counts, and no deduction can take you below the minimum wage. Ask for the amount back in writing, naming the date and the sum; if they refuse, ACAS is free to ring and an employment tribunal claim for an unauthorised deduction has to be started within three months less a day of the deduction.

If it is one tap and the rest of the house runs, it is that tap's own supply: the isolation valve on the pipe under the sink is a slot-head screw, and a half turn the other way is the usual answer. With the valve open, unscrew the spout aerator and soak it in vinegar - a scaled-up aerator stops a tap dead. If every tap is dry, it is the stopcock where the mains comes in, or the supply itself, so check the water company's postcode status before you pay anyone. A tap that runs and then stops is an airlock: hold your palm over the spout and open it fully for a few seconds, or back-fill it with a jug from another tap. And if the pipe is in a cold wall in freezing weather, warm it gently with a hairdryer - never a blowtorch - with the tap left open.

If it is somewhere nobody goes, leave it: a wasp nest dies in autumn and is never reused. If it is by a door or someone in the house is allergic, pay a local pest controller, usually 50 to 80 pounds, rather than going up a ladder with a spray - and do not block the entrance, because they will find another way into the house.

If it's faulty they have to take it back, whatever their returns policy says: ask for a refund, or a repair or replacement if they refuse. For a change of mind, their own returns terms decide, so check what you agreed to when you bought it.

Ignore the "extreme" number and look at the comfort rating: a 2 or 3 season bag rated to about 0C comfort covers British camping from spring to autumn, and a 3 season one is the usual first buy. Down is lighter and packs smaller but useless once wet, synthetic keeps some warmth damp and is cheaper and washable, and a mummy shape is warmer for its weight than a rectangular one. The mat under you decides how warm you sleep as much as the bag does, so spend there too.

Ignore it rather than nag: most children stop on their own between two and four, and the fuss is what keeps it going. Praise the times they are not doing it, offer a cuddly or a fidget at the moments they usually suck, and put a plaster on the thumb for a week if they want to stop. Only past five, when it is pushing the teeth or the palate out of line, is it worth a word with a dentist - and bitter paint is not recommended.

In physics a vacuum is a space with no matter in it at all, or as close as anyone gets: there is no air in space, and a thermos flask keeps its heat by holding a vacuum between two walls. It is also why a vacuum cleaner's fan can push air in.

In England the fee is £9,250 a year, so a three-year course is about £27,750, and living costs add roughly £9,000 to £12,000 a year on top. Nobody pays it up front: it is a loan repaid at 9% of what you earn above about £25,000, and what is left is written off after 40 years, so the monthly figure matters far more than the headline. Check the maintenance loan for your household income, and pay the deposit for accommodation out of the first instalment rather than a credit card.

In England they can leave school at 16 but not stop learning: education or training has to continue until 18, and a college course, an apprenticeship or a job with accredited training in the week all count, so it does not have to be more school. The realistic routes are A levels at a sixth form, a level 2 or 3 vocational course (BTEC, T level, NVQ) at college, or an apprenticeship, which is a paid job with the training built in and usually one day a week at college. Visit one college open day together before deciding, and ask about a level 2 course if the GCSEs are shaky, because that is a stepping stone to level 3 rather than a dead end.

In England you register with Ofsted, or a childminding agency, before you take payment for looking after a child under eight for more than two hours a day. You need an enhanced DBS check for yourself and every adult over 16 in the house, a 12-hour paediatric first aid course, insurance and about £35 to register, and an inspector visits your home. No more than six children under eight at once, three of them under five.

In England and Wales a straightforward estate usually gets probate six to twelve weeks after you send the forms. The long pole is the inheritance tax return: over the 325,000 pound threshold the IHT400 comes first and can add months. Apply yourself through the government probate service when the will is simple; a solicitor earns the 1,500 to 3,000 pounds if there is a house, a business or a disagreement.

In England and Wales a fence or a garden wall can be 2 metres high without planning permission, or 1 metre where it is next to a road, footpath or driveway; conservation areas, listed buildings and some new estates have stricter rules, so ring the council's planning desk before going higher. On a boundary you also want the neighbour's agreement, because a fence over 2 metres can be complained about as a nuisance even where the height itself is allowed.

In England a child starts reception in the September after their fourth birthday, and school is compulsory from the term after they turn five. Apply through your council by 15 January in the year they start, and you hear on 16 April. A summer-born child starts at four and a bit, a September-born one close to five. Scotland and Wales use different dates.

In the microwave a cob takes 3 to 4 minutes on full power for one and 5 to 6 for two: leave it in its husk, or wrap it in a sheet of damp kitchen paper, and turn it once halfway. Give it a minute to stand before you butter it, because it carries on cooking. Loose kernels in a covered bowl with a splash of water take 2 to 3 minutes, stirred halfway, and frozen sweetcorn the same plus a minute.

In the print dialog open Layout (or More settings) and choose Print on Both Sides, flipping on the long edge, which is what reads like a book; on a Mac it is the Two-Sided tick in the Copies and Pages sheet. If there is no such option, the printer has no duplexer and will ask you to take the paper out and turn it over.

In the EU it is free to use your normal allowance, but only on plans that include it: several UK networks charge a flat fee for EU roaming again, usually about £2 a day or £10 a month, so check your own plan before you go. Outside Europe assume £5 to £10 a day unless you buy a travel add-on first, and turn data roaming off for the flight so nothing connects on the way over.
In the Six Nations a Grand Slam is winning all five of your matches in the same season, which also brings three bonus points; a Triple Crown is one of the home nations beating the other three.

In the UK the return for a tax year is due by 31 January, about ten months after the year ends, and the bill is due the same day. If you cannot pay, still file on time: the late-filing penalty is immediate, while a payment plan with HMRC is something you can ask for online.

In the UK the words are used much the same way - someone trained to listen and help you work something through. "Therapist" is the broader word and covers CBT and other set approaches; "counsellor" usually means a trained listener rather than a clinician. Neither title is protected by law, so check the person is accredited.

In the UK the flu jab is free on the NHS if you are 65 or over, pregnant, or have a condition like asthma, diabetes or a weak immune system, and for some carers and young children. At 45 without one of those you would pay, about 15 to 20 pounds at a pharmacy, and it is worth it if you would rather not lose a week to flu. Best asked for in the autumn.

In the UK they are rarely worth it unless you drive on ungritted country roads or in Scotland: winter tyres grip much better below 7°C, but most people do fine on good all-season tyres. If you do fit them, put all four on and swap back in spring, because they wear fast in the warm.

In the UK you can give blood from 17 to 65 if you have not donated before, and you need to be at least 50kg; men can go every 12 weeks and women every 16. Wait 7 days after a cold or flu, and 4 months after a tattoo, piercing or acupuncture. Most everyday medicines are fine - the questionnaire at the session decides, and staff will tell you there and then. Book at blood.co.uk; a whole donation takes about an hour including the rest afterwards.

In the UK, eggs with the British Lion mark are fine raw or runny, even for pregnant women, babies and older people, because the hens are vaccinated. Eggs without the stamp should be cooked until the white and yolk are solid. Anything with raw egg in it - mayo, mousse, homemade ice cream - should be kept in the fridge and eaten within a day or two.

In the UK, £8 to £12 an hour is usual, more in a city and more for several children or a late night. Agree the hourly rate and a minimum of two or three hours before the first evening, because a two-hour job that fills the evening is worth the same as a longer one. Ask two local sitters what they charge, and add a little for after midnight.

In the UK an employer is not obliged to give one unless your contract says so or a regulator does - banks, care work and teaching are the usual exceptions - and a plain no is lawful. If you do give one it must be fair and accurate, so stick to dates, title and facts you could stand behind in front of the person. A short no is safer than a half-hearted yes.

In the UK a pedal-assist e-bike up to 250W and 15.5mph is legally an ordinary bicycle: no licence, no tax, no compulsory insurance, and cycle paths and towpaths are open to it. A throttle that pulls you without pedalling, or assist past 15.5mph, makes it a moped, and then the licence, insurance, helmet and number plate do apply. Trains, ferries and bike racks usually take them but the operator sets the rule, and several ban them at peak times.

In the active voice the doer comes first: the dog ate my homework. In the passive the thing done to comes first: my homework was eaten. Active is usually shorter and clearer; passive earns its place when the doer doesn't matter or you'd rather not name them.

In the amount most people eat, sugar is not poison, but it is the easiest calorie to take in unnoticed and the main cause of tooth decay. It is habit-forming rather than addictive like nicotine. Brown sugar is white sugar with molasses: same calories, same limit. Keep free sugars - the added sort, plus honey, syrup and juice - under 30g a day, about seven teaspoons, which one can of Coke uses up. Whole fruit is the exception: the fibre slows it down.

In the email app tap the attach or paperclip icon, pick Photos and choose the picture; a phone usually offers a size and Small or Medium is plenty for a snapshot. Most services stop at about 20 to 25MB, so for several photos send a link from Google Photos or iCloud instead of attaching them.

In the freezer, about 3 months for most things before the quality drops: raw meat and fish, cooked dishes, soup, stock, bread, cake, cheese and butter. A whole bird or a joint goes 6 months, blanched veg and fruit 6 to 12, and ice cream 2 to 3. It stays safe long past that, just drier, so write the date on the bag. The fridge is much shorter: raw meat 1 to 2 days, cooked food 3 to 4.

In Gmail: the gear icon > See all settings > General, scroll to Signature, create one and save, and it is added to new mail and replies. In Outlook: Settings > Mail > Compose and reply > Email signature. Keep it to your name, a phone number and one line of what you do; a logo image often shows as an attachment on other people's phones.

In Google Drive or OneDrive, right-click the file or folder, choose Share, then set the access to Viewer and copy the link - a link on its own only works for people already signed in to your account. For photos, share the album rather than each picture. For a document two people are working on, Share and add their email as Editor instead.

In Google Maps tap your picture > Offline maps > Select your own map, frame the area you need and download it; it stays usable for about a year and works with the phone in airplane mode. On an iPhone, Apple Maps keeps recent routes offline and a dedicated app such as Organic Maps covers the same ground for free.

In 1605 a group of English Catholics, including Guy Fawkes, planned to blow up Parliament and King James I with barrels of gunpowder. The plot was discovered on 5 November, which is why Britain still has bonfire night.

In WhatsApp open the group, tap the name at the top, scroll down and tap Exit group; muting it instead (Mute notifications) keeps you in without the noise, which is usually the better move for a family group. On an iPhone in Messages, open the conversation, tap the faces at the top and choose Leave this Conversation. You can also just mute it for a year and nobody is told.

In WhatsApp it is Settings > Privacy > Read receipts, and switching it off means you stop seeing theirs as well as them seeing yours. On an iPhone it is Settings > Messages > Send Read Receipts, which can be off for everyone or on for one contact only. Blue ticks that stay grey can also just mean they have not opened the chat.

In Word or Excel use File then Save As (or Export) and pick PDF; on a Mac, File then Print and choose Save as PDF from the bottom of the print box, which works in any app; on a phone, tap Share then Print and pinch out on the preview to turn it into a PDF, or just send the page to yourself and choose PDF. A scanned sheet is the same idea in the Files or Notes app, which saves straight to PDF.

In autumn the colony is winding down: the queen stops laying, so the workers have no grubs to feed and go looking for sugar instead, which is why they crowd round jam, fruit and bins in September. They are not nastier, just hungry and idle. They die at the first hard frosts, only the new queen survives, and the old nest is never reused.

In biology, a niche is the job a species does where it lives: what it eats, when it is active, where it shelters and what eats it. Two species with the same niche in one place compete, and one usually wins or moves away.
In cakes, yes: use 80g of oil for every 100g of butter, and expect a slightly denser crumb. Not in pastry or shortbread, and not where you cream butter and sugar for air.

In cakes and biscuits, one egg becomes 60g of yoghurt, half a mashed banana, or a tablespoon of ground flax or chia stirred into 3 tablespoons of water and left 10 minutes. Those bind but do not lift, so add half a teaspoon of baking powder. For glazing or binding mince, a little milk or oil does the job.

In cakes and biscuits, margarine at the same weight, or a neutral oil at about three-quarters of the weight. For frying and greasing, any oil will do. Do not swap the butter in pastry, shortbread or buttercream, where its taste is the whole point.

In chemistry a suspension is solid bits mixed through a liquid that do not dissolve and settle out if you leave it: muddy water, or flour stirred into water. Shaking it mixes it again, which is how it differs from a solution.

In British English the noun is practice and the verb is practise: piano practice, but I practise every day. Advice and advise work the same way: advice is the thing, advise is what you do. In American English practice does both jobs.

In 501 both players start at 501 and count down, and you finish on a double or the bullseye — going below the target or landing on one is a bust and the turn is wiped. That is why players aim for treble 20s early and switch to a tidy double once they are under 170. Three treble 20s in one visit is 180, the highest score there is.

In a rented home the landlord must have the gas appliances and flues checked every 12 months by a Gas Safe registered engineer and give you a copy of the record within 28 days of the check - it is their duty and their cost, and a copy should be there when you move in. You cannot do the check yourself - only a Gas Safe registered engineer can sign the record - and a home you own needs no certificate by law, so a yearly boiler service is the thing to book instead.

In a slow cooker a 2kg chicken takes 4 to 5 hours on low, or 3 hours on high: sit it on a few balls of foil so it is not stewing in its own juice, and do not add water, as it makes plenty. Check the thigh juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75C before you take it out.

In a browser or a document, Ctrl and + makes it bigger and Ctrl and - smaller, and Ctrl and 0 puts it back to normal; on a Mac it is Command and those keys. To change the size of everything on the machine, Windows has Settings > Accessibility > Text size and a Mac has System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Text size.

In a British city park in winter you'll usually see robins, blackbirds, blue tits, great tits, pigeons, crows and magpies, with gulls and starlings on the grass. Look in the bushes and bare trees rather than the open lawn, and early morning is the busiest time.

In a fraction the numerator is the top number, the one being counted, and the denominator is the bottom number, the one that says how many equal pieces the whole is cut into. In 3/4 the numerator is 3 and the denominator is 4, so you have three of four equal pieces.

In fog use dipped headlights and, only when visibility is under about 100 metres, your rear fog light - and switch it off as soon as it clears, because a bright rear light in thinning fog dazzles the driver behind and hides your brake lights. Slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see, leave a big gap, and do not follow the tail lights in front too closely, since they lead you into the same crash. Hazard lights are for a stopped queue, not for moving in fog.

In law, black men in the United States got the vote in 1870 with the 15th Amendment, and black women with the 19th in 1920, but in the South poll taxes, literacy tests and violence kept most of them off the roll until the Voting Rights Act of 1965. In South Africa everyone of every race voted for the first time in 1994.

In marinades and dressings: sour cream, creme fraiche or buttermilk. In baking: milk with a teaspoon of lemon juice, left 10 minutes. In a curry, stir any of them in off the heat, or they split into grains.
In maths the range is the gap between the smallest and largest number: for 3, 7, 9 and 15 it is 15 - 3 = 12. Put the numbers in order first, then subtract the smallest from the largest.

In maths a variable is a letter standing for a number you do not know yet, or one that can change, such as x in 3x + 4 = 19. You work with it as if it were a number, then solve to find what it must be.

Income tax and national insurance pay for the things nobody can buy alone: the NHS, schools, roads, the state pension, the police, and benefits for people who cannot work. It comes out of your pay before you see it, in bands: the first £12,570 a year is tax free, then 20p in the pound up to £50,270 and 40p above that. For a child: everyone chips in a little so the hospitals and roads work for all of us.

Income tax is taken from your pay before it reaches you. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland you pay nothing on the first £12,570, 20% from there to £50,270, 40% up to £125,140 and 45% above, and Scotland has its own five bands. On a £30,000 salary the tax is about £3,486 a year, and a tax code on your payslip is what tells payroll how much to take.

Insects, worms, spiders and caterpillars for most of the year, then berries and fruit in winter when the ground is hard. That is the moment to put out mealworms, suet and a few sultanas, and a robin will take them from a hand within a couple of weeks.

Insects, carrion, seeds and fruit, plus eggs and nestlings in spring, which is why small birds mob one and why a garden with a magpie nesting goes quiet for a few weeks. It also takes scraps and pet food left outside.

Insects, caught on the wing by echolocation: a single pipistrelle eats around 3,000 midges and mosquitoes in a night, which is why bats over a garden mean fewer bites. Fruit bats in the tropics eat fruit and nectar instead.

Insects and worms from lawns and dung, then fruit, seeds and scraps; in autumn they switch to berries and orchards, which is when the murmurations gather before roosting. A starling will also take fat balls and kitchen scraps from a feeder.

Insoles help a foot that rolls in or an arch that aches, and on their own they do little for knee pain - so it depends what is hurting. A running shop will watch you run for free and tell you whether you overpronate, and a cheap pair with a firm arch is a fair first try: if the pain is worst in your heel with the first steps in the morning that is plantar fasciitis, and a heel cup with a firmer arch usually eases it over a few weeks. Do the strength work too, because insoles support a foot rather than fix it - calf raises and picking a towel up with your toes, most days. See a podiatrist rather than guessing if you are diabetic, if the pain is sharp and one-sided, or if two months of the cheap ones has changed nothing.

Install Gmail or Outlook and sign in with the address and the password: it brings in the last 30 days and then keeps syncing, and both apps hold several accounts at once. If it is a work address, ask IT for the settings rather than guessing, because it usually needs a Microsoft or Google sign-in, not just a password.

Install Google Photos or iCloud Photos on both and let it upload, then they are on the laptop without a cable. For a one-off, plug the phone in and open it as a drive: on Windows it appears under This PC, on a Mac use Image Capture. Copy, check the count matches, and only then delete from the phone.

Instead of plain flour, self-raising is the usual stand-in: use it at the same weight and leave out the baking powder the recipe asks for, or add a teaspoon less. Bread flour works in cakes and scones too but drinks more liquid, so add it a spoonful at a time. For thickening a sauce, cornflour at half the amount does the job better.

Into the pension first, as far as the employer's contribution goes: they have to add at least 3% on top of your 5%, and the tax relief adds another 20% of what you pay, so nothing a savings account offers comes close. Above that, a stocks and shares ISA is the more flexible place, because pension money is locked up until 55 (57 from 2028). Keep three to six months of bills in an easy-access account whatever else you do, and if you are self-employed a private pension or a SIPP gets the same tax relief.
Iron with a little carbon in it - under about 2% - and the stainless kind also has chromium, which is what stops it rusting. The carbon is the part that makes it hard: pure iron is soft and bends.

Iron-deficiency anaemia shows up as tiredness, breathlessness on the stairs, pale skin and sometimes a sore tongue or brittle nails. A simple blood test at the GP confirms it, and iron tablets with vitamin C usually fix it in a couple of months, but the cause is worth checking too - heavy periods and a poor diet are the usual ones.
Isaac Herzog is the president of Israel: in office since 2021. The job is ceremonial - the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, runs the government.

Isotopes are versions of the same element with different numbers of neutrons, so the same chemistry but a different weight. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both behave like carbon, but carbon-14 is unstable and decays at a steady rate, which is how archaeologists date old bone and wood. Some isotopes are radioactive enough to be useful in medicine and power, and some are harmless.

It sprays hot water and detergent at the dishes from arms that rotate, then rinses and dries the load with the heat of the last rinse. The salt softens hard water so the detergent can work and the rinse aid makes the water run off instead of drying in spots; neither cleans anything by itself.

It switches off every radio at once - mobile data, wifi and Bluetooth - so the phone cannot transmit, which is why planes ask for it. It is also the fastest fix for a phone that has lost signal: turn it on for ten seconds and off again, and it re-registers with the network. You can switch wifi back on while it is on, so a flight's wifi still works.

It takes about twenty minutes for the fullness signal to arrive, so a meal eaten in five leaves you looking for more afterwards. Put the fork down between mouthfuls, drink water with the meal and eat at a table without a screen - those three do more than any rule about chewing a set number of times.

It tumbles the clothes through warmed air, and the damp air is either blown outside through a vent or cooled so the water condenses and collects in a drawer. A heat-pump dryer heats that air again instead of dumping it, so it uses about half the electricity and takes longer.

It usually means they want room to think, not that they are leaving - give them the room they asked for and keep one light line open. Ask once, calmly, what they need and roughly how long for, then let them come back to you: chasing the answer in the first days is what turns a pause into a break.

It barely matters: twenty minutes on the counter warms the meat by a couple of degrees inside, so the middle still cooks the same. Leaving raw meat out for hours is a food safety risk. What does make a difference is patting it dry and seasoning it just before it goes in the pan - a dry surface browns, a wet one steams.

It cannot go behind your eye - that one is a myth: it has folded up under the upper or lower lid. Wash your hands, put in a couple of saline or rewetting drops and blink, then look up, pull the upper lid gently down over the lower lashes and look down; the lens usually slides out onto your cheek. If it is still there, slide it with the pad of a clean finger to the white of the eye where it is easier to pinch, and lift it off between thumb and forefinger - never a nail, tweezers or a cotton bud. Still stuck after half an hour, or the eye is painful, red or your sight has gone blurred, go to an optician or eye casualty the same day and take your lens case with you. Don't sleep in it.

It depends on the medicine, and your diabetes team sets the number for you: on insulin most people test before every meal and again two hours after, plus before bed and before driving, which lands at four to ten times a day. On tablets or on nothing, two or three times a week at different times of day is plenty for many people, and some only need it before breakfast. A sensor reads all day without a prick, and the tablets that raise the risk of a low are the ones that need the most checking. Ask them at your next review rather than guessing, and write down what you get so a pattern shows.

It depends on the animal. A dog is usually done at about six months, and the bigger the breed the later: a large or giant dog is often left to nine or twelve months, a small one at five or six, and a bitch before her first season or three months after one ends rather than in the middle of it. A cat at four to six months, a female from about four, before her first litter. A rabbit at about four months for a buck and five or six for a doe, and both before they are bonded rather than after. There is no upper limit either, so an older animal can still be done and the vet will weigh the anaesthetic against the reason. Nothing says you must, so it is a choice as well as a date: ask your own vet what they would do for your animal, because the timing is a conversation, not a rule.

It depends on the crystal, and the make and model tell you which: acrylic or Hesalite (many older and cheaper watches) polishes out at home with a dab of Polywatch or Brasso on a soft cloth, a mineral glass one wants a jeweller with cerium oxide - about £15 to £30 - and a sapphire crystal only scratches on a diamond or a brick, so a mark that will not lift is usually the anti-reflective coating. A scratch you can feel with a fingernail is a new crystal, £30 to £80 fitted, and worth doing before damp gets in.

It depends on the device: an iPhone is the side button and volume-up together, most Android phones are power and volume-down, a Windows PC is Windows key + Shift + S, and a Mac is Shift + Command + 4 to drag a box. Say which one you are on and I will give you the exact steps for it.

It depends on what you want to do: for nursing, engineering, law or teaching the degree is the door, and for plenty of other jobs experience gets you further for less money. Compare a degree with a degree apprenticeship in the same field — earn while you learn, no fees — and look at what people actually doing the job you want studied. Ask two of them before deciding.

It falls apart for three reasons: the mince is too lean, it was handled too much, or it was turned before it had a crust. Use mince with some fat in it (20 per cent is right), break it up with a fork rather than squeezing it, and add an egg and a couple of spoons of breadcrumbs per 500g if the meat is lean - then shape it loosely, press a shallow dip in the middle and chill it 20 minutes so it sets. Salt it just before it goes in the pan, cook it in a hot pan and leave it alone for 3 minutes before the first turn, and it will hold.

It fills the drum, tumbles the clothes through hot water and detergent, then spins them fast so the water is flung out through the holes. Detergent lifts grease off the cloth and the paddles in the drum do the rubbing, which is why an overfilled drum comes out still dirty - the clothes cannot move.

It goes on weight and size, not distance: Royal Mail prices a letter and a large letter off the thickness, and a parcel off its weight and whether it fits a small, medium or large box. A small parcel by second class is a few pounds, first class a pound or two more, Signed For a couple more again, and anything over 2 kg is usually cheaper with a courier - put the weight and size into the Royal Mail price finder or ask at the counter, and take a photo of the scales. Prices change every April.

It goes in waves and it takes months, and that is not you failing at forgiving: trust comes back from consistency, not from a promise. Months of them doing what they say and being where they say does more than any reassurance, so agree what openness you need for now and put an end date on it, or it turns into a life. Counselling gives you a place to say the hard things without it becoming a row, and it is fine to say you have not decided yet. Rushing to forgive is the thing that tends to fail.

It is named for the flower the bees worked: clover and acacia are light and mild, heather and chestnut are dark and strong, and orange blossom is perfumed. Runny or set is the same honey - set has simply crystallised, which a warm jug of water undoes. Raw or unfiltered means it has not been heated, so it is cloudier and tastes more of the flowers. Never give any honey to a baby under one, because of the botulism risk.

It is nearly always the weekly distance going up too fast: keep the increase under about a tenth a week and hold it steady every fourth week. Run most of it easy enough to talk in full sentences, with one faster session and one longer run, and do two short strength sessions a week for calves, glutes and hips, which is what covers most running injuries. The same pain in the same spot three runs in a row is a physio visit, not a new pair of shoes.

It is on a plate or sticker you can read without moving the machine: on a boiler, under the case near the pipes, behind the drop-down flap or on the side panel, and the Benchmark sheet in the manual carries the same serial. On a washing machine or dishwasher it is on the rim inside the door, on a fridge or freezer inside on a side wall or the inner door, on an oven on the frame or the door edge, and on a kettle, toaster or microwave underneath. The model number is the short code and the serial is the longer one - the parts shop or the maker's site wants both, so photograph the plate once you have found it.

It is paint gluing the sash to the frame: run a sharp knife, held flat, round the join between the frame and the opening sash to cut the paint film, then work a thin scraper or a wide chisel gently into the gap and ease the window open rather than forcing the handle. Once it is open, sand the paint off the meeting faces and rub a candle or silicone spray along them. Never lever against the glass.

It is probably asleep or on the wrong display, not dead: press a key, then try the brightness keys and Ctrl+Alt+Del, and if the fan is still running, hold the power button for ten seconds to force it off and back on. On a laptop, plug in an external monitor or shine a torch at the screen - if you can see a faint image, the backlight has failed and the screen needs replacing.

It is sweat and skin cells trapped under the strap, and rubber and silicone ones hold it worse than leather: take the watch off to sleep and wash the strap with warm water and a little washing-up liquid or soap, then dry it properly before it goes back on, because damp is what keeps the smell. A paste of bicarbonate of soda left on for ten minutes takes out the rest, and a fabric strap goes in a mesh bag on a cool wash. Leather will not take a soaking: wipe it with a cloth wrung out in diluted vinegar and dry it away from heat.

It is the part of student finance that pays your rent and food, and it is paid to you, not the university: roughly £10,000 a year if you live away from home outside London, around £13,000 in London, and less if you live with your parents - check the figure for your year on gov.uk, because it moves. How much of it you get depends on your household income, so two people on the same course get different amounts. You repay it only once you earn over the threshold, then 9% of what is above it, and the balance is written off after around 40 years.

It is the period when a club can register new players: a long summer window, roughly June to the start of September, and a short one through January. Outside them nobody can move, which is why deadline day is frantic.

It is the power setting, not a fault: on Windows, Settings > System > Power & sleep, set Screen to never and Sleep to never while it is plugged in; on a Mac, System Settings > Lock Screen > Turn display off on power adapter, set it to never. Windows also has a separate setting for the lock screen timeout under Personalisation > Lock screen > Screen saver, and a laptop on battery will still sleep by design.

It is the same legally binding wedding, minus the venue: in England you give notice at your local register office (£46 each) and the ceremony at the register office itself costs about £57, against several hundred for a registrar to come to a hotel. You need two witnesses, the notice has to be given at least 29 days ahead, and the ceremony can be as short as you like, so the money can go on the meal or the honeymoon instead.

It is the small claims track of the county court, and it is built for people with no solicitor: in England and Wales a claim up to £10,000 goes online at moneyclaims.service.gov.uk, in Scotland it is simple procedure up to £5,000, and in Northern Ireland small claims up to £3,000. The court fee is on a scale - £35 for a claim up to £300, rising to about £455 at £10,000 - and you get it back if you win. Write first: a dated letter before claim saying what is owed, why, and a deadline of 14 days. Most settle at that letter, and the online form is the same work either way.

It is the Maillard reaction: past about 140C the sugars and amino acids on the surface rearrange into hundreds of new flavour compounds, and that is the brown crust and the savoury smell. Pat the surface dry first, get the pan properly hot, and leave space, because steam from a crowded pan keeps everything at boiling and it goes grey instead.

It is the air, not the lime: a cut avocado browns where oxygen reaches it, and the greenest guacamole is the one with the least air in it. Press cling film right onto the surface in a shallow tub, keep the stones in if you like, and a squeeze of lime plus a pinch of salt slows it. If it has already browned it is still fine to eat - stir the top layer in and it looks green again.

It is the fridge's colder twin - a pump circulates a refrigerant that expands and gets very cold, taking heat out of the air, and the heat leaves at the back. Because it holds food far below 0C, the water in it turns to ice, and ice keeps almost all the food's water locked up, so the bugs that spoil food cannot grow.

It is usually the remote or a timer in the set: take the batteries out of the remote for a night, and look in Settings for a sleep timer or an auto power-on. If it comes on when you switch something else on, that is HDMI-CEC (Bravia Sync, Anynet+ or Simplink), and turning that off stops the TV following the console or the soundbar.

It is usually under the kitchen sink where the cold main comes up, or in a box near the boundary outside, and it is a brass tap that closes clockwise: turn it a quarter turn at a time, run the cold tap to check it has stopped, and turn it back anti-clockwise afterwards. If it is seized, don't force it with a wrench - a rounded stopcock means turning the water off at the road, which is the water company's job.

It is worth it only if your supply is properly hard - over about 250mg of calcium carbonate per litre, which your water supplier publishes for your postcode - and if the scale is costing you money: a kettle that furs up and a shower head that clogs. Expect a few hundred to well over a thousand pounds fitted, plus a bag of salt a month, and a bypass tap for drinking water because it adds sodium. For a kettle and a shower head alone, a filter jug and a bottle of descaler cost far less and do most of the work.

It is written on the car: the inside of the fuel flap, the inside of the fuel cap and the handbook all say 'unleaded 95' or 'diesel' in so many words, and the filler neck is the backstop, because a diesel nozzle will not fit into a petrol car. Most petrol cars want standard unleaded (E10, 95 RON) and the handbook only asks for 98 if the engine needs it - putting 95 in a car that wants 98 costs a little power and economy, which is not the same as damage. Petrol in a diesel is the expensive one: stop before you start it and it is a drain and flush, start it and it is a fuel pump.
It is always two words: a lot. 'Alot' is not a word, so if you would write 'a lot of 'people' or 'a lot better', put the space in.

It is asking after sleep, and that is a setting: on Windows, Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options > 'If you've been away, when should Windows require you to sign in again?' and choose Never; on a Mac, System Settings > Lock Screen and turn off 'Require password after screen saver begins'. If it asks for a password you do not know, that is the account password, so use the reset link on the sign-in screen rather than guessing.

It is bacteria eating what the wash leaves behind - sweat, body oil and skin cells - and they are not all removed by a cool quick wash, which is why a garment can smell the moment it warms up again. Keep it between about 20 and 80 per cent where you can, and avoid heat more than anything: a phone left on a hot dashboard loses capacity faster than one charged carefully. Slow charging overnight is fine, fast charging now and then is fine, and there is no need to run it flat or to charge it to 100 per cent to keep it honest - both are old advice for batteries that no longer exist.

Keep it cool and keep it off 100%: heat is what ages a laptop battery, so use it on a hard surface with the vents clear, and switch on the maker's charge limit (80% in the Mac or Lenovo settings, Battery care in Asus) if it mostly lives on a desk. A laptop battery lasts three to five years; expect about 500 to 1000 full charges before it drops to 80% of new.

Keep it dry, keep it on and keep it up: a bin bag taped over the top - or a proper cast cover - gets you in the shower, a bag of frozen peas over a tea towel on and off for the first couple of days does the swelling, and wiggling the fingers or toes a few times an hour keeps them working. The itch is the worst part and the answer is not a knitting needle, a pen or talcum powder down the top: blow cool air down it, tap the outside, or ask the plaster room. Ring the fracture clinic the same day if the fingers or toes go white, blue or cold, tingle, or will not move, if the cast is rubbing a sore spot, or if it splits, cracks or gets soggy - a wet or loose cast is redone, so do not pad it out yourself. A musty smell with pain is a phone call too.

Keyhole surgery is an operation done through two or three small cuts rather than one long one: a slim camera goes in through the belly button, the surgeon works off the screen, and the cuts are each a centimetre or so, closed with a stitch or glue. The operation takes about as long as the open version but the recovery is much shorter - often home the same day or the next, back to light normal in a week. The gas they use to make room is what leaves you with a bloated ache in the shoulders for a day or two.

Kidney stones are crystals of salt in urine, and most pass on their own: drink two to three litres of water a day - enough that your urine is pale - take paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain, and sieve your urine if you have been asked to catch the stone. A stone under about 5mm usually comes out within a few weeks, and the pain eases as soon as it moves into the bladder. Go to A&E the same day if the pain is not controlled by painkillers, you have a fever or shivering, you cannot pass urine, or there is blood and you feel unwell - a blocked kidney with an infection is an emergency. Once it is out, ask what the stone is made of, because the diet that keeps the next one away depends on the type, and cut back on salt meanwhile.

Kim Jong Un has led North Korea since 2011, when his father Kim Jong Il died. He is not the head of state on paper: the constitution gives that title to the president of the presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly, Choe Ryong Hae. The Workers' Party is the only party that decides anything.
King Salman is the king of Saudi Arabia, but his son Mohammed bin Salman - crown prince, and prime minister since 2022 - runs the country day to day.

Knead it 10 minutes by hand, or 5 to 8 minutes in a mixer with a dough hook: it is ready when it is smooth, feels a little tacky, and springs back when you press a finger in. The real test is to stretch a piece thin enough to see light through it without it tearing.

Kneeling is the one thing many people never get back after a knee replacement: the new knee can take it, but the skin over it is numb and sore against a hard floor, so most people kneel on a cushion for a few minutes at a time rather than rule it out - try it on something soft once the wound is fully healed and the swelling has gone down. After a hip replacement you can kneel, but get down on the operated knee first and keep the new hip from bending past 90 degrees for the first few months. If kneeling is for gardening or a job, ask the physio to practise it with you rather than finding out on the day.

Knock once, politely, at a reasonable hour and assume they don't know: say what happens and ask for the one change you want, in a sentence - 'this has happened three nights running now, can we sort it out?' Going in friendly keeps it a small thing. If it continues, keep a short log and ask the council or landlord for help rather than escalating yourself.

Know the route and aim to be ten to fifteen minutes early - not earlier, and never late; if you are ahead of that, wait in a cafe rather than the lobby. The night before, put the clothes out, print the job description and your notes, charge your phone and note the name of whoever you are meeting. Eat something before you go: a hungry interview is a shaky one.

Know which valve you have: a Presta valve is the thin one and its little nut has to be unscrewed and tapped to let air in, while a Schrader is the car-type one a pump just pushes onto. Pump to the range printed on the sidewall and use a track pump with a gauge at home, because no thumb can feel 60psi. Top up about once a week: a tyre loses a little air all the time, and a soft one pinches flat on a kerb.
Kyriakos Mitsotakis is the prime minister of Greece: in office since 2019 and re-elected in June 2023, leading New Democracy. The president, a ceremonial role, is chosen by parliament.

LED stands for light-emitting diode: a chip of semiconductor that gives out light when current passes through it, with no filament to burn out and very little heat at the glass. That is why an LED bulb lasts years and uses a fraction of the power of an old filament bulb, and why it is cool enough to touch.

LOL stands for laugh out loud, and it is usually doing the job a nod does in speech: it says the message landed as a joke, not that anyone actually laughed. That is why people write it at the end of a line rather than the start.

LPA stands for lasting power of attorney: the legal document that lets someone you choose make decisions for you if you cannot - about money and property, or about health and care. It has to be registered with the Office of the Public Guardian while you still have the capacity to make it, and it costs £82 per document in England and Wales.

Label a shelf and one tub of your own, then say it once, face to face: "I'm happy to share milk and bread, but I'd rather the rest was mine" is something a person can agree to, and a note on the fridge is not. Agree a shared shelf for the things you both use, and if it carries on, ask to split the shopping bill rather than policing the fridge.

Labyrinthitis and vestibular neuritis are inflammation of the balance nerve, nearly always after a cold: sudden spinning vertigo with nausea, worse when you move your head, and it is vestibular neuritis if the hearing is normal and labyrinthitis if it is muffled. It is not usually dangerous but it is horrible, so see the GP the same day the first time it happens to have it checked. Anti-sickness tablets such as cyclizine from a pharmacy get you through the first few days, then gentle movement and walking help the brain retrain the balance - lying still for longer slows recovery. Go to A&E if there is weakness down one side, slurred speech, double vision or a sudden hearing loss.

Lamb is done by temperature in the thickest part: 55C is pink, 60C is medium, 70C is well done, and it is juiciest if you take it out 5C under and rest it 10 minutes. A leg roasts 25 minutes per 500g at 180C (160C fan) plus 25 minutes on top, and a chop takes 3 minutes a side for pink.

Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know. Be honest with yourself - this buys a pass, not understanding.

Lateness is nearly always the plan rather than the person: time one real journey at the hour you actually travel and add ten minutes, then set an alarm for leaving rather than only for waking. Lay out clothes, bag and keys the night before, and book the one earlier train instead of telling yourself you will hurry. If it is the last five minutes that keep going, drop the one job you do on the way out: being five minutes early costs nothing.

Latex sap from the rubber tree, for natural rubber: it is tapped out of the bark, then mixed with sulphur and heated, which links the chains so it springs back instead of staying sticky. Most car tyres are synthetic rubber made from oil.

Latitude is how far north or south of the equator a place is, in degrees from 0 at the equator to 90 at the poles: London is about 51 north, and your latitude is what sets how long the days are and how warm the place gets.

Laughter is mostly social: people laugh far more with someone else there, and it signals that a threat or a mistake is harmless, which is why nervous giggles and contagious laughter happen. It releases tension and bonds a group, and there is no single joke centre in the brain.
Lava is molten rock that has come out of a volcano onto the surface; the same stuff underground is magma. It cools into rock, and runny lava flows far while thick lava piles up near the vent.
Lawrence Wong is the prime minister of Singapore: in office since May 2024, when Lee Hsien Loong stepped down after twenty years. The PAP has governed since independence in 1965.

Lay mineral wool 270mm deep, which is two layers of 100mm plus one of 70mm criss-crossed, and it costs about £300 to £600 for a typical semi if you do it yourself: it is the cheapest thing a house can do to its bills and pays back in a few years. Keep the eaves clear at the edge for ventilation, do not squash the wool down, and leave a gap round downlights unless they are marked fire-rated. Bigger jobs - a flat roof, a dormer, spray foam - want someone registered, and there are often grants.

Lay turf in spring or early autumn, when the soil is warm and wet: clear and dig the ground, level it, tread it and rake it, then put a straight edge down and lay the rolls brick-fashion, butting them tight. Water the whole lawn as you go and keep it damp for a fortnight: the turf has no roots in the soil until it knits. Or order it early in the week and lay it the day it arrives - a roll left in the shade goes yellow in a day or two.

Lay bacon rashers on a rack over a tray and bake at 200C (180C fan) for 15 to 18 minutes: crisp, flat and no splashing. In a pan, start it in a cold pan on a medium heat so it renders before it burns.

Lay it top-down: three or four split logs on the grate, a handful of kindling crossed on top, two firelighters, then light the kindling and leave the air control wide open for ten minutes before you close it down. A fire that will not catch is nearly always damp wood, kindling that is too big, or the air shut too early - small dry wood first, bigger on top, and heat the flue before you expect a flame.

Layers pellets or mash as the base, about 120 g a day per hen, plus grass, weeds, insects and vegetable scraps; grit and crushed oyster shell keep the eggshells hard. Bread, pasta and corn are treats rather than feed, and avocado, citrus peel, salt and anything mouldy are not for them at all.

Layers and nothing tight: soft trousers or leggings, a t-shirt with a jumper you can take off, and slip-on shoes for security. Compression socks are the one thing that makes a long flight feel better, and a scarf doubles as a blanket.

Lead with what you have done, not with job titles: school or college, volunteering, a paper round, a team you played in, a club you ran. Then a two-line profile at the top saying what you want and what you are good at with people, numbers or tools. One page is plenty - employers reading a first CV look for effort, not titles.

Leaning back is fine and nobody thinks worse of you, but do it slowly and check behind you, because it can land on someone's laptop. Avoid mealtimes if you can, and don't keep it back for the whole flight in the front row of economy.

Learn these twelve and you can get through most of a holiday: hello, goodbye, please, thank you, sorry, excuse me, do you speak English, I don't understand, how much is this, the bill please, where is the toilet, and help. Say them out loud until they are automatic, because under pressure you will use what you can say without thinking.

Learn five movements and ignore everything else for a month: squat, hinge (deadlift), push, pull and carry. Two or three sessions a week, three sets of 8–12, adding a little weight each time. Book the induction: a trainer checks your form once and shows you the machines, and it's usually free.

Leather gives about half a size; suede, patent and anything synthetic give nothing, so a shoe that pinches your toes is the wrong size and a shoe that is merely snug will loosen. For snug leather, wear thick socks, warm the shoe for 30 seconds with a hairdryer on low and walk round the house until it is cold, or spray the inside with half rubbing alcohol and half water and wear it for 20 minutes; for one tight spot take it to a cobbler, who stretches it on a proper last for about £10 to £20. Send back anything unworn that pinches, and try the wider fitting in the same size before you go up a whole size.

Leave only for a reason that still holds on a good day, and only once you could afford the gap. Three tests decide it. First, is it the work or the place: if you would do the same tasks somewhere else without the dread it is the place, and a move inside or out is cheaper than a career change. Second, is the thing you want fixable where you are - hours, a manager, a project - and have you asked for it in one plain conversation. Third, can you afford the gap: three months of money you could live on, and a CV updated before you need it. If two of the three are still bad after one honest attempt at the fix, start looking while you are still there. Set a date now and decide on it, not on a Tuesday when it is unbearable.

Leave some of the liquid out and put something solid in instead: half a banana, a spoon of Greek yoghurt, oats or peanut butter, or a handful of frozen fruit, then blend it again. Pour the milk or juice in last, a splash at a time, until it moves the way you want - ice waters it down, so keep it to a few cubes.

Leave the wine out and use the same amount of hot stock, plus a squeeze of lemon or a teaspoon of white wine vinegar so it still tastes bright.
