Stir or turn them over at halfway, and stand for a minute before you lift the cover, because the steam is hotter than boiling water. Stop while they are still bright and a knife goes in with a little resistance - they carry on cooking as they stand.

Put the alarm across the room so you have to stand up, and set it for the last minute you can actually get up: snoozing for nine minutes at a time just restarts the groggy part. Going to bed 30 minutes earlier fixes the reason you want to snooze better than any alarm app.

Put the alarm across the room and take the first one for a week, even when you are tired: the nine extra minutes cost you the deep sleep at the end of the night and leave you groggier. If mornings are brutal, go to bed half an hour earlier that week.

Put the ask in one message with a deadline and a default: "I need a yes or no on the budget by Friday; if I don't hear back I'll go with the cheaper option." If it's urgent and they're swamped, ask their assistant or agree a 10-minute slot at the end of the stand-up; chasing the same unanswered email harder rarely helps.

Put the bowl or the jug on the scales first, press tare - or the zero button - and then add the flour, so the display counts only what you put in; press it again for the next thing and the bowl never has to come off. Weigh the wet things first and the dry ones after, because a scale cannot tell you what you have already added. A scale with a 1g step is the one to own: a 5g step cannot measure 7g of yeast.

Put the box on the paper and pull it up each side to see how much you need: enough to come up and over with about 3cm to spare, no more. Tape the long seam first, crease the folds with your thumbnail, then do the ends - fold the two corners in to make a triangle, fold the point up over the box, and tape it flat. Work on the floor with the tape stuck to the table edge so you are not hunting for the end, and use a bag for anything awkward (a bottle, a helmet, a bike): a neat bag looks better than a lumpy parcel and takes ten seconds.

Put the clove on the board, lay the flat of a wide knife on it and press down hard with the heel of your hand until it splits; pull the skin off, chop it, then drag the knife across the pile a few times with a pinch of salt and it turns to paste. The bottom of a glass or the back of a spoon crushes it just as well, and the fine side of a grater gives you a purée for a sauce.

Put the complaint in writing, list what's wrong and ask for it fixed within 14 days before paying anything more. If they don't, report them to Trading Standards through Citizens Advice and use the small claims court for what you've lost.

Put the cue ball just off the side cushion and hit the outside of the pack thinly with screw, so the cue ball comes back up the table and tucks behind baulk rather than sitting in the open. A soft, thin contact brings a red out to the side pocket for the next shot, and the safety is the point: the break-off is not a shot to win the frame with. Do not hit the pack straight on, because that leaves the cue ball in the middle.

Put the headphones in pairing mode (usually hold the power button until a light flashes), then open Bluetooth in your phone's settings and tap the name when it appears. If it is not listed, delete the old pairing from the phone and start again.

Put the hole of the protractor on the point of the angle and line the 0 line up with one arm, then read the number the other arm crosses - use the scale that starts at 0 on that side, so the two rows of numbers do not fool you. Under 90 is acute, over 90 is obtuse, and exactly 90 is a right angle.

Put the key in one place that you walk past on the way out - a hook inside the front door - and nowhere else, because the pockets, the bag and the coat are what lose it. A spare with a neighbour or family is free and saves the locksmith, and a key safe by the door (about twenty pounds, screwed on, with a code) covers the rest. If you rent, ask the landlord for a second key: yours to pay for, and almost always allowed.

Put them to work rather than down the sink: a handful of used grounds goes in the compost or round plants that like a little acid - blueberries, camellias, hydrangeas - and a small dish of dry ones in the fridge takes up smells for a couple of days. They also make a gritty paste for a stained sink or a scorched pan, and a weak brew poured over the garden is fine once it is cold. Keep them out of the drain, where they set like cement, and off seedlings in a thick layer, which stops water getting through.

Put them back in the case with the lid open and hold the button on the back (AirPods) or the case (most others) until the light flashes, because they only appear in the Bluetooth list while they are in pairing mode. If they are still not there, forget the old entry in Bluetooth, then hold the case button for 15 seconds to reset them and pair again. One bud that will not charge is usually a dirty contact in the case.

Put what you want in the first line, then the facts in date order, then a deadline. "I'm writing about the damp in the back bedroom at 14 Elm Road, which I reported on 3 March. Could you send someone to look at it by 20 March?" Name the address or the reference, keep it to one page, and say what you'll do next if nothing happens. Keep a copy, and send it by email or recorded post so you can show when it went. Ringing as well often gets an answer sooner than the letter does.

Put your postcode into the parliament.uk "find your MP" page, or theyworkforyou.com, and it gives the MP for your address with their email and constituency office. Their contact details are also on the council's website, and a library or Citizens Advice will look it up if you would rather ask someone.

Put your postcode into the parliament.uk "find your MP" page, or theyworkforyou.com, and it gives the MP for your address with their email and constituency office. Your councillor for the ward is on your council's own site under your postcode, and they are the faster route for bins, housing and roads - the MP is for benefits, visas and anything a government department has to answer.

Put your postcode into your council's recycling centre page - searching your postcode and "recycling centre" lands on it, and gov.uk links every council's site finder - and that page has the opening hours, what the site takes and whether you have to book. Take something that proves you live in the area, because most sites check it at the gate, and book a slot first if your council runs a booking system, which the busiest ones do at weekends.

Put your attention on the other person instead of on yourself, because awkwardness is mostly the spotlight turned inward. Have two questions you can ask anyone ('What have you been up to this week?', 'How do you know Sam?'), give one small thing back so it is a swap rather than an interview, and let yourself leave when you have had enough - a short good conversation beats an evening of wishing you had stayed home.

Put cleaner under the rim and leave it 10 minutes, then scrub right round the bowl with a toilet brush, including under the rim, and flush. A limescale ring at the waterline comes off with a citric acid or vinegar soak overnight.

Put a non-slip mattress pad or a piece of rubbery shelf liner under it, cut to the frame, and push the mattress back hard against the headboard before you put the sheets on. A bed frame with a lip or a box base holds it better than slats, and if there is a gap at the foot, a rolled towel between mattress and frame stops the creep. Smooth bedding slides more than cotton or linen, so a fitted sheet tucked right under the corners helps too.

Put a proper anti-slip underlay under it, the open-weave rubber sort, cut a couple of centimetres smaller than the rug, or run double-sided carpet tape along the edges: on a shiny floor the sticky corner pads do the job too. A rug that curls wants the curled end face down on the floor with something heavy on it overnight, or warmed with a hairdryer while you press it flat.

Put a warm flannel on it for ten minutes three or four times a day and cover it with a clean dressing, and do not squeeze it: most boils come to a head and drain on their own in a week or two. Take paracetamol if it throbs, and wash your hands after touching it or the dressing, because the germ spreads. See a GP the same day if the redness is spreading, the skin around it is hot and swollen, you have a fever, or the boil is on your face or near the top of your nose; also get it looked at if it is bigger than a golf ball, if you have diabetes, or if you keep getting them, because a course of antibiotics or a small drainage is sometimes needed.

Put a bowl of water with a slice of lemon in for 3 minutes on high, then leave the door shut another 5: the steam loosens everything and it wipes off. Never run it empty and never put metal in, and unplug it before you scrub the inside.
Put a comma before but when it joins two full sentences: "I wanted to come, but my train was cancelled." When it only pairs two words or short phrases - small but strong - leave the comma out.

Put a little cider vinegar or red wine in a glass with a drop of washing-up liquid: they fly in and sink. Then take away what they are breeding in - the ripe fruit (into the fridge for a week), the bottles and the bin, and the plughole, which gets a kettle of boiling water at night. The glass catches the rest in a day or two.

Put every date in your phone's calendar once, with the reminder two weeks before as well as on the day: two weeks is the point at which you can still post a card or book a table. Keep a few blank cards and stamps in a drawer, so the reminder turns into something you can do there and then rather than another thing to remember later.

Put it on one page tonight, because the unknown is usually bigger than the number: what comes in each month, what goes out on the things you cannot avoid, and every debt with its minimum payment and its rate. Then pick the smallest thing you can do this week - a payment plan with the council or the energy company, or one call to a free debt service (StepChange, National Debtline or Citizens Advice in the UK), which costs nothing and does not touch your credit file. Give the worry a fifteen-minute slot in the evening and write one line to take to it, so it stops arriving at 3am: postponing is the part that trains it. If it is most days for months, or you cannot sleep for it, that is worth a GP appointment too.

Put it in the dampest room with the door and windows shut, on a flat surface and a hand's width from the wall so air can get at it - a landing or a hallway rarely is the dampest room, and a dehumidifier there just dries the air that leaks out of everywhere else. Keep it off a cold loft or garage floor in winter, where the coil ices up and it spends its time defrosting instead of drying. Empty the tank before it stops itself, or fit the hose and let it drain into a sink or a bucket.

Put it in writing the same day and take dated photos of the work: what you agreed, what is wrong, what you want put right and by when, and say you are holding the balance until it is done. Give them 14 days to come back and fix it. Then use the levers you already have: a trade body scheme (FMB, TrustMark, Which? Trusted Traders) has a dispute service, a card payment over 100 pounds is a section 75 claim with your bank, and money owed up to 10,000 pounds goes through the small claims track online without a solicitor. A tradesman who took a deposit and vanished is a police matter, so report it and keep every message.

Put it in writing to the right department and give them the facts they can act on: the address or street, the date, a photo or reference number, and what you want done - potholes and pavements to highways, noise, bins and fly-tipping to environmental health, a repair in a council house to the repairs line with your tenancy number. Use the online form or their email so there is a record, keep a copy and note the date. If nothing happens in ten working days, chase it and ask for it to be logged as a formal complaint; after their final reply the Local Government Ombudsman takes it on free.

Put it in writing to the landlord - a dated email or letter, what happened, what you want done and a deadline of 14 days - and keep a copy, because every later step asks for it. If a letting agent runs the flat, the agent has to belong to a free redress scheme (the Property Redress Scheme or The Property Ombudsman), and a complaint can go there after eight weeks, or sooner if the agent deadlocks it. A hazard - damp, no heating, a broken boiler, a fire risk - is your council's housing team, who can inspect and order the work, and the deposit scheme holding your deposit sorts out a deposit argument. Shelter or Citizens Advice will read the letter before you send it, free.

Put it in writing today: the dates, the hours and the amount you should have had, sent to your manager and to payroll, and keep a copy - a text or email is a record, a phone call is not. Check your contract for the pay date and take screenshots of your payslips and bank account. If the next payday also misses, ring ACAS's free helpline and ask about a claim for unauthorised deductions at an employment tribunal, which you have three months less a day from each missed payment to start. If the company has stopped trading, the Insolvency Service can pay what you are owed.

Put it in writing with photos and dates, and ask them to find the cause rather than paint over it: a coat of paint is the one repair that makes damp come back. If they will not act, your council's environmental health team can inspect damp and mould as a hazard to health and make the landlord deal with it, and Shelter or Citizens Advice will help you write the letter free. Keep paying the rent and keep copies of everything you send. A window open for ten minutes a day and a dehumidifier hold it while you wait.

Put it in writing with a date: 'The rent for March hasn't come through - can you send it by Friday?', or if you want the room back, 'I need it from the first of next month.' Decide what happens if they don't act before you send it, and check the tenancy agreement for who the landlord can actually chase. Say it in week one rather than month three - it only gets harder.

Put it in writing, dated, and keep a copy: say you are leaving on the date your notice runs out - a month on a rolling tenancy in England, two on a fixed term with a break clause - and that it should end on the day the rent is due. Ask them to confirm the end date in writing, and book the deposit return, the final meter readings and the council tax move for that day.

Put it in writing before anything else: say what is wrong, what you want - it fixed, or your money back - and give a deadline of 14 days, by email so there is a record. If they are in a trade body, its free dispute service can step in; otherwise send a letter before action and use the small claims court, which is cheap and settles most of these. Photograph the work and keep the quotes, texts and receipts, and pay any balance on a card so the bank can help.

Put it in a cardboard box with air holes in the lid, somewhere warm, dark and quiet, and leave it an hour or two: most come round and fly off. Do not feed it or try to give it water, and do not keep it longer than a few hours - one that is still there after that wants a wildlife rescue or a vet. Wash your hands afterwards. Then stop the next one: something on the outside of the glass, because a pane reflects the sky and the birds fly at it.
Pyjamas after two or three nights: they sit against your skin all night, so they pick up sweat and skin cells faster than a shirt does.

QR stands for Quick Response, and the name is the only thing about it that is simple: the square holds up to about four thousand characters of text, which is how a whole web address fits in, and it survives being printed small, smudged or half covered. That is why the one on a bus stop still scans from a photograph.

Quails want a hutch or aviary with a solid floor, a deep layer of bedding and somewhere to hide, and a pair or a small group rather than one. Gamebird crumb with extra calcium for layers, and a low roof: they fly straight up when startled.

Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901, 63 years, and gave her name to the age. She had nine children, married Prince Albert, and after he died in 1861 spent years in mourning, which is why so many photos of her look the way they do.

Quiche keeps 3 days in the fridge, covered, and eat it cold or reheat it to piping hot all the way through rather than warm. A quiche freezes for 2 months, cut in slices and wrapped: thaw it in the fridge overnight and warm it through. Once the egg custard smells sour or the top has a sheen of water, it is done.

Quick things for both, with the oven at 200C fan: puff pastry makes sausage rolls, cheese straws, palmiers, a tomato and goat's cheese tart, or a sheet folded over sliced apple as a rough tarte tatin. Filo makes spanakopita, samosas, little cigar rolls of feta and spinach, and baklava - keep it under a damp cloth while you work, because it dries out in a minute. For either one, heat the empty tray in the oven first, get the filling already cooked and cooled, brush the top with beaten egg, and don't open the door for the first 15 minutes or it sinks. Spare sheets freeze well: wrap them tight and they thaw in about 20 minutes.
Quiet means little noise - a quiet street. Quite means fairly or completely - quite good, quite sure. The e and the t swap places, so check which word you meant, not which one looks right.

RNA is DNA's working copy: the same four-letter code, but single-stranded and short-lived. A cell copies the gene it needs into RNA, carries it out of the nucleus and builds a protein from it, which is why a cell can keep its DNA safe and still make what it needs. Some viruses, including the cold and flu viruses, store their instructions as RNA instead.

RRP stands for recommended retail price: the price the maker suggests, not one a shop has to charge. Shops often sell below it, so a crossed-out RRP is a marketing figure - compare what you would actually pay elsewhere rather than the saving on the label.

RSVP stands for repondez s'il vous plait, French for please reply, which is why the letters have no apostrophe and no full stops. An invitation that wants numbers for catering will usually give a date; reply by then even when the answer is no, because a maybe costs the host a place.

Rabbit and rodent teeth grow all their lives and hay is what wears them down: unlimited hay, some leafy greens and a wooden block to gnaw, and skip the muesli mix. Drooling, wet chin or refusing food means the teeth need the vet before they stop eating altogether.
Rachel Reeves is the chancellor of the exchequer - Labour, in office since July 2024, and the first woman to hold the job. The chancellor writes the budget and sets the tax rules.

Radiators that are hot at the bottom and cold at the top have air in them: open the bleed valve at the top with a radiator key, a quarter turn at a time, with a cloth under it, until water trickles out steadily. Two minutes a radiator is all it takes, and a whole house takes ten to fifteen minutes. Then check the boiler pressure and top it up if it's below 1 bar.

Radioactivity is what unstable atoms give off, rays or particles, as they settle into a steadier state: it happens on its own and cannot be switched off. It powers a nuclear plant, and the tiny amount in a smoke alarm is what sets it off.

Radiotherapy is a beam of X-rays aimed at one small area to damage the cells growing out of control, and each session is short - about 10 to 20 minutes, with the treatment itself only a few minutes. It does not hurt and does not make you radioactive; you lie still on a couch under the machine, usually every weekday for a few weeks, and the planning session before the first one takes longer than the treatment. Tiredness and sore skin over the area build up over the course, and your team gives you the cream and the rules.
Radishes are ready about four weeks after sowing, at marble size: pull one to check rather than waiting for the row. Left longer they go woody and hot, so sow little and often instead of one big row.

Radishes keep 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge once the leaves are off, because the leaves pull the water out of the root; put them in a damp tea towel or a bag in the salad drawer. A soft, bendy radish crisps up again in iced water for 20 minutes. Split or slimy ones are past it.

Rain soaks into the ground and runs into rivers, and your tap water is drawn from a river, a reservoir or a borehole, then filtered and treated so nothing can grow in it and pumped to the house under pressure. A town near hills is usually fed from a reservoir; anywhere else it comes from a river or from deep underground.
Ras el hanout is a Moroccan blend and not usually hot - cumin, coriander, cinnamon, ginger and pepper - though some jars have chilli in. A tablespoon for a tagine or a tray of vegetables.
Raspberries ripen from July: pick when the berry comes away from its core with no tug, and eat or freeze them the same day, because they keep a day at most. Autumn kinds crop on into October.

Raw mince keeps 1 to 2 days in the fridge, on the bottom shelf in a bowl so nothing drips, and freezes for about 3 months; once it is cooked, a bolognese, chilli or shepherd's pie keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Cook it on the day you buy it, or freeze it that day and thaw it in the fridge overnight - it is the food to be strictest about, because mincing spreads bacteria right through the meat. Grey-brown on the outside is only oxygen and is fine; grey all through, slimy, or sour-smelling is not.

Raw fish is safe to eat if it has been frozen first - 24 hours at -20C kills the parasites, and that is what sushi-grade fish has had - so a fresh fillet from a fishmonger eaten the day you buy it is fine for most people, and a supermarket fillet is not meant for it. Skip raw fish altogether if you are pregnant or your immune system is weak, and never eat freshwater fish raw.

Reach it rather than move it: a duster or a microfibre cloth taped to a broom handle gets behind a radiator or under a low bed, and a vacuum crevice tool does the same afterwards. If the thing can be pulled out - a fridge, a washing machine, a sofa without a fixed back - pull it clear first and clean the wall and the floor behind it, because that is where crumbs and dust collect. While the fridge or the freezer is out, vacuum the coil or grille at the back: dust on it is why it runs hot and costs more.

Reactor 4 at Chernobyl exploded on 26 April 1986 during an overnight safety test, and the graphite fire burned for days, spreading radiation across Europe. About 30 workers and firefighters died of acute radiation within weeks, and the 30km exclusion zone is still there.

Read the minimum term and the exit fee before you do anything, because an early exit can cost most of what is left on the contract. Ring or write to cancel, ask for the final bill and give a meter reading on the day - a photograph of the meter is enough - and keep the date and the name of whoever you spoke to. Do not cancel an energy account before the switch: sign up with the new supplier and it takes over on a set date. For broadband, send the router back if it was theirs, or they bill you for it. Then check the next two statements, because an account that keeps billing after it was cancelled is the commonest complaint there is.

Read the name of the charge on the statement first, because they are different problems: an unarranged overdraft fee, a bounced direct debit, a card fee abroad and a monthly account fee all have different fixes. Ask for the first one back - banks have to treat you fairly, and most refund a first unarranged overdraft charge if you ask in the app or on the phone, before it becomes a complaint. Then stop the next one: turn on a low-balance text alert, set the direct debit for a day after payday, and check whether the paid overdraft or the packaged account fee is buying anything you do not already have, because both can be cancelled. If the bank refuses, ask for the complaint to be logged and take it to the Financial Ombudsman, which is free.

Read the packet: plenty of chicken and beef stock cubes are actually vegetarian, and plenty of 'vegetable' gravies have meat fat in them. The vegetarian ones are labelled, and a vegetable stock cube with a dash of soy sauce covers the same ground.

Read the term and the exit fee first: a minimum term normally lets you leave early for a set fee, often a share of what is left, and anything signed online or over the phone has a 14-day cooling-off period. Then ask in writing whether it can be transferred, downgraded or paused instead of cancelled, and if they refuse, the free ombudsman for that industry will look at it after eight weeks.

Read the black digits only and ignore anything after the decimal point or in red - those are the fractions of a unit, and a supplier only wants the whole numbers. A gas meter counts cubic metres if it says m3, or hundreds of cubic feet if it says ft3 on an older one, and the bill needs to agree which. An electricity meter may show one row of numbers, or two for day and night if you are on Economy 7: send both. Take a photo on the first of the month and send it in, because a reading you send beats an estimate.

Read the break clause first: a fixed term often lets you leave after six or twelve months with two months' written notice. Without one you owe the rent until the term ends unless the landlord agrees, so ask in writing and offer to cover the re-letting costs, usually cheaper than paying to the end. Never post the keys back and stop paying: the debt follows you.

Read the envelope: if it names only you, or says one seat, it is just you - a plus one is only a plus one when the invitation says so or the host names your partner. Asking straight is fine and better early: "Is there room for a plus one?" If the answer is yes, remember the meal and the seat were counted for two from then on.

Read the fee off the league's own handbook rather than a round number: grassroots referees in England are paid a match fee by the competition - around 30 to 45 pounds for an adult Saturday game - plus mileage, and the level above is a good deal more. Ask the league secretary what the fee and the travel rate are before your first appointment.

Read the ingredient list for the four that catch people out: rennet (animal, in hard cheese), gelatin (pork or beef, in sweets and jelly), anchovy (Worcestershire sauce, Caesar dressing) and lard or suet (pastry, some bread). The Vegetarian Society logo, a green V or the words 'suitable for vegetarians' settle it faster than any list, and 'may contain fish' means the same fryer or the same factory rather than an ingredient.

Read the lender's letter or app for the new rate and the date it started: a payment jumps either because your fix has ended and you are on the standard variable rate, or because a tracker followed the base rate. If the fix has ended, ask a broker for a new deal now - remortgaging usually takes six to eight weeks and is far cheaper than drifting. If the new payment is only just too much, ask the lender to extend the term before you miss anything.

Read your tenancy for a break clause first: it is the term that lets either side end the tenancy before the fixed term is up, and it names the date it can be used and how much notice it takes, often two months. Without one the landlord only has to agree if you cover the rent until a new tenant moves in, so offer to find one and put that in writing - you cannot usually just hand back the keys. On a rolling monthly tenancy in England you give one month's notice and the landlord gives two, and it has to end on the day the rent is due.

Read it once for what it says and once only for mistakes, and change the order - bottom to top, or aloud - so your eye stops filling in what you meant. Check names, dates and numbers against the source, then the four usual slips: its/it's, your/you're, then/than, and missing words.

Read it out loud, or have your computer read it aloud: the places you stumble are the places to fix. Cut every "very", "really" and "basically", make sure each paragraph's first sentence says its point, and check names, dates and quotes — those are what get marked down.
Recep Tayyip Erdogan is the president of Turkey: in office since 2014, and prime minister before that from 2003. The presidency became the centre of power after the 2017 referendum.

Red, white and rosé are about the skin, not the grape: red is fermented on it, white off it, and rosé briefly on it. Sparkling is a second fermentation for the bubbles, and fortified - sherry, port, madeira - has spirit added, which is why it keeps for weeks after opening. The other axis is the grape and where it grew, which is what makes a Chablis lean and a Chardonnay from a hot place buttery, and a wine dry or sweet.

Red means stop, and there is no turning left on red in the UK, whatever the road you are joining. Amber also means stop unless you are so close that stopping would be dangerous. Jumping a red is three points and a £100 fine, and cameras catch it whether or not anyone else is there.

Red meat is more forgiving than chicken: a grey-brown colour on the outside of a chop is just air and it is fine, but a sour or putrid smell, a sticky tacky surface or green patches means bin it. Raw beef, lamb and pork keep 3 to 5 days in the fridge, mince only 1 to 2.

Register online at the government's register to vote service: it takes about five minutes and needs your date of birth, address and National Insurance number. Do it again after every move - the register does not follow you - and the deadline is 12 working days before an election. The same page has a check for whether you are on it, and being on it also helps your credit score.

Register when your sales go over £90,000 in any rolling twelve months, or when you think they will in the next thirty days; do it within 30 days of the end of the month you went over. Registering means you add 20% VAT to your prices and hand it over, but you also reclaim the VAT on what you buy for the business, so if your customers are other businesses it usually costs you nothing. Returns are normally quarterly and have to be filed from digital records. You can ask to deregister if your sales fall under £88,000.

Register as a sole trader with HMRC once you start trading, and at the latest by 5 October after the end of your first tax year. Do it online at gov.uk: HMRC posts a UTR number, which every tax return and invoice needs. Then file by 31 January and pay Class 2 and Class 4 National Insurance through the return.

Reheat it until it is piping hot all the way through, not just warm at the edges: a splash of water, a lid on, and a stir halfway so it heats evenly. In a microwave, cover it, heat in one-minute bursts, then let it stand two minutes; in a pan or an oven it wants about 20 minutes at 180C. You can reheat leftovers once only - chicken and rice are the two to be strictest with - so heat what you are going to eat and bin the rest.

Remortgaging is worth it when a new deal beats your current rate by enough to cover the costs, which are usually £1,000-£2,000, so a drop of about 0.5% or more normally does. Start looking three to six months before your current deal ends and check the early repayment charge first.

Renew it online on the driving agency's site (gov.uk in the UK) with a new photo: it costs about £14 to £17 and usually arrives within a week. You can normally keep driving while the renewal is being processed, under what is called section 88, as long as your doctor has not told you to stop and the licence was not taken away rather than simply expired.

Repair it in the first ten minutes, not at the weekend: say sorry plainly, name the moment "I snapped about the dishes" with no but after it, and say what you will do instead. Then look for the pattern rather than the person - most snapping is hunger, sleep or a thing you have not said out loud, at the same time of day. Agree a word you can both say, like "I'm at my limit", that means one of you leaves the room for ten minutes and nobody follows. Tell them the real thing earlier, too: "I'm not cross about the bin, I'm shattered" ends more rows than an apology does. If it has become name-calling, or either of you is frightened, that is worth talking to someone outside the two of you about.

Reply the same day with the trade-off, not a complaint: "If this lands on Thursday, testing slips to Monday - which would you rather?" If the dates keep moving, say it plainly at your next one-to-one: "I plan around the dates I'm given, so once we agree a date I need it to hold." Put the risk in writing once; a missed deadline you flagged early is a much smaller problem.

Reply to the court instead of ignoring it: the form with the letter takes a plea and a statement of your income, and the court sets a fine you can pay in instalments from that. Nobody is jailed for a first missed payment - the prison warning is about not replying at all - and if you cannot pay what was set, ask the court to look at your means again rather than skipping it. A council tax summons is not a criminal record, and paying before the hearing usually stops the extra costs.

Reply to the invite, not the person's face: "I can't add value to the whole hour - can I come for the first ten minutes, or send my bit in writing?" Give a reason about the work and offer the smaller version in the same sentence, so nobody has to chase you. If it is a standing meeting that no longer needs you, ask for your slot to go: "Anything for me in the weekly? Happy to drop off and read the notes."

Reply by the date on the card, and answer both things they asked in one line: yes or no, and the meal or dietary bit. "Thank you so much - we'd love to come. Two of us, one vegetarian, no allergies." If the invitation names you alone, go alone: asking to bring someone is the one thing that puts a host in an awkward spot. A no is fine and better early: "Thank you for thinking of us, but we can't make it - I hope it's a wonderful day."

Report it to reception in writing the moment you notice and ask for a copy of the report. A hotel in England and Wales is only liable for up to £50 an item and £100 in all, and only for their carelessness, so valuables are covered only if you handed them in for safe keeping and got a receipt. If something was taken from the room, get a crime reference and claim on your travel or home insurance.

Report it to the police within 24 hours if the other driver drove off, and get a crime reference number. Then tell your own insurer even if you are not claiming, because the policy usually requires it, and see whether the car park or a nearby house has CCTV before it is overwritten.

Report it to the council the same day: a missed bin is free to report, the form is on their waste page, and most rounds come back within two working days. Leave the bin out at the kerbside where they can reach it, note the date and any reference, and if it happens twice photograph the full bin and note when the lorry came past - a repeat miss is usually a round that changed and nobody told you.

Report it to the council's environmental health team the same day: they inspect the kitchen, and that report is what makes a claim stick. Keep the receipt, the packaging and any leftovers, and get a doctor to record it if you are still unwell. Claim in writing for the days you lost and for the illness, first from the restaurant and then through the small claims court, which has a three-year limit.

Report it to the council's environmental health team, who handle smoke, smells, dust and fumes from a farm, a factory, a takeaway or a building site: ring them or use the online form with the address and the times it happens, and keep a diary for a week or two. If it is bad enough they must look into it as a statutory nuisance and can serve an abatement notice, so ask for the case reference. Nothing in ten working days means chasing it and asking for it to be logged as a formal complaint; after their final reply the Local Government Ombudsman takes it on free.

Report it to the highways team of the council that owns that road - not the police or the parish - using the map form on their website: drop a pin, add a photo and keep the reference number it gives you, because a fixed reference is what makes the next report count and it is the first thing a claim asks for. Street lights, kerbs and pavements go to the same team. If it damaged a tyre or a wheel, use the council's own claims form with the repair invoice and two quotes: the council can defend itself by showing it inspected the road on schedule, so your earlier reference is the strongest thing you hold.

Report it to the local police the same day and ask for a written report with a crime number: insurers and the consulate both want one, and some forces will not give it later. Then ring your insurer's 24-hour line, cancel any cards that were in the bag, and if the passport has gone book an emergency travel document at the nearest consulate. Keep receipts for what you had to buy.

Report it at the airline's desk in the baggage hall before you leave, with the bag tag and your boarding pass, and do not go home without a written report and a reference number: that number is what every later claim and refund hangs on. Ask what they will pay for clothes and toiletries in the meantime and keep every receipt. Most bags turn up within 24 to 48 hours; if it has not after 21 days, claim for it as lost.

Report it at the airport before you leave, at the airline's baggage desk: you get a PIR reference, and nothing is paid without one. Then claim in writing - 7 days for damage, 21 for a delay - and the airline owes up to about £1,300 per passenger, plus what you had to spend on essentials with the receipts.

Resistance is how much a material fights the current, measured in ohms: a thin, long, hot wire has more of it than a short thick cold one, which is why a laptop charger stays cool and a toaster element glows. Ohm's law ties the three together, voltage equals current times resistance, so at 12 V a 4 ohm resistor carries 3 A. It turns the energy into heat, which is the point of a heater and the reason a long cable warms up.

Respiration is how cells release energy from glucose: glucose plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water plus energy, and every cell does it all the time. Breathing is only the moving of air in and out - the oxygen it brings is used in respiration and the carbon dioxide it carries away was made there. Sprinting, or holding your breath under water, outruns the oxygen, so muscles switch to anaerobic respiration, which makes energy fast and leaves lactic acid: that is the burn.

Respite care is a break for the person doing the caring, and it comes in small pieces: a few hours a week at a day centre, somebody sitting with them so you can go out, or a week in a care home so you can have a holiday. Arrange it before you are desperate, because the good places have a waiting list. The council can arrange it after a carer's assessment and means-tests the person you care for, not you; hospices and charities often have free day places and short stays; and the GP or district nurse knows what exists locally, which is usually more than the council website says.

Rest, drink plenty and take paracetamol or ibuprofen to bring it down; there's no need to strip off or sponge with cold water. Get advice the same day for 38C in a baby under three months, or a fever with a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade under a glass, breathlessness, confusion or not drinking.

Rest, fluids and paracetamol are the treatment for a cold; it usually clears in about a week, and the cough can linger for two or three. Honey in warm water eases a cough, and see a GP if you are getting worse after a week, short of breath, or coughing up blood.

Rest it, ice it for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours for the first two days, wrap it firmly and keep it up when you sit, then start gentle movement as the pain allows. A simple sprain settles in one to three weeks. If you cannot put weight on it, it is very swollen or the pain is over a bone, get it looked at the same day.

Restart the box or the set at the wall and leave it a minute - a slow channel change is nearly always the software in the set-top box rather than the aerial. If the menus are slow too, free up the set's storage and uninstall apps you do not use; a retune is worth one go if only some channels are slow.

Restart it when it asks, and once a week if it never does: that clears the memory leaks and half-installed updates that make a machine feel tired. Shut down properly from the Start menu or the Apple menu rather than holding the power button, which is the same as pulling the plug and can leave files half-written.

Restart it first, then clear space: Settings > General > iPad Storage lists what is taking the room, and an iPad with almost no free space slows down badly. After that, Settings > General > Software Update - and if it is an old one on the newest system, that is usually the honest reason.

Restart it first, then clear space: a phone that is nearly full slows down badly, so delete old videos and apps you do not use. On Android, clearing the cache in Settings > Storage helps too; on an iPhone, check Settings > General > iPhone Storage for the app taking the most.

Restructures run on written criteria, so ask HR for the pools, the criteria, the timetable and the minutes, in writing. Apply for the roles that exist instead of waiting to be placed, and answer the criteria in their words with an example and a number. Do not resign before the outcome - it can cost you redundancy pay; check the contract and the statutory minimum. Take a union rep into the consultation meeting if you have one, and ring ACAS, which is free, the same week.

Retention is the slice of a building job's price the client keeps back as insurance that the snagging gets done - 5% is the usual figure, sometimes 3%. Half of it is released when the job is finished to the contract's standard, and the other half after a defects period, usually twelve months, once anything that has gone wrong has been put right. It should say all of that in the contract, with the date each half is due; if it does not, ask for it in writing before you start, because a builder who has not read the term will not expect the last payment to wait a year.

Retune from the set's own menu: Settings > Channels > Auto tuning on most sets, and on a Freeview or Sky box from its own menu instead - the box is the one to retune if the set's channels are fine. Push the aerial lead back in at both ends first, and retune again a day later after transmitter work. Channels that moved number or vanished overnight are a retune, not a broken aerial.

Rheumatic fever is the body reacting to an untreated strep throat or scarlet fever two to four weeks later: a fever with painful, swollen joints that move around, sometimes a rash and a racing heart, and it needs a GP the same day because it can scar the heart valves. The protection is treating a sore throat with the antibiotics the GP prescribes and finishing the course, so a sore throat with a fever and swollen neck glands in a child is worth having swabbed rather than waited out. It is now rare in the UK but still seen in children aged 5 to 15.

Rheumatoid arthritis is the immune system attacking the lining of the joints, and it is treated early and hard because most of the damage happens in the first year or two: a rheumatology team starts disease-modifying drugs such as methotrexate, with a short course of steroids to settle a flare, and those are what keep the joints working. Keep moving between flares, take the tablets even when you feel well, and tell the team the same day if a joint is hot and swollen or you feel generally unwell, since that can be an infection rather than a flare and the two want opposite treatment.

Rice on its own is about 130 calories per 100g cooked and not fattening: what goes with it and how much of it decides that. A mug of cooked rice, about 150g, is a normal portion, and brown rice has around three times the fibre of white.

Rice grows in a paddy: a field walled to hold a few inches of water, planted with seedlings and flooded for most of the season. It wants heat and a lot of water, which is why so much of it comes from Asia.

Rice left out at room temperature is the one leftover worth being strict about: bin it after 2 hours. Cooked rice can grow a toxin that reheating doesn't destroy, so cool any leftovers fast, fridge them within the hour, and eat them within a day.

Ride easy miles before hard ones: three or four rides a week with one long steady one, spinning at 80 to 90 turns a minute in a gear you can hold. Add one session of 4 x 5 minutes hard with 5 minutes easy between, and put the hills in the long ride. Check saddle height first - a saddle too low costs power and sore knees.

Ridges that run up and down the nail are normal and get more common with age - they are the nail equivalent of a wrinkle and need nothing. Lines that run across the nail after an illness, nails that curve up like a spoon, or pitting like a thimble are worth a GP or pharmacist look, because they can point at iron or thyroid, and a dark streak that does not grow out is seen within two weeks.

Right-click the folder > Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder on Windows, or right-click > Compress on a Mac, and a single .zip file appears beside it to attach to the email. Photos and videos shrink a lot, documents barely change, and an email usually stops around 20 to 25MB, so a big video needs a transfer link instead.

Right-click an empty part of the desktop and choose New > Folder on Windows, or right-click and choose New Folder on a Mac, then type a name. In a file window the shortcut is Ctrl + Shift + N on Windows and Shift + Command + N on a Mac.
Right. What have you tried so far?

Ring practices near you and ask straight out whether they take new NHS patients, because the lists open and close. If none do, ring 111: they can find an urgent NHS appointment within 24 hours, and you do not have to be registered anywhere to be seen. An NHS check-up is £27.40 in England, and a dental school or a community clinic is cheaper still.

Ring the DWP on 0800 917 2222 and say you want to claim PIP - there is no online form - and from that call to a decision is usually two to four months. They post out a long form about how your condition affects you day to day, and you have a month to send it back with any evidence you have: letters from a GP, consultant or therapist, and a diary of a bad day. You can claim from 16 up to state pension age, and the difficulty has to have lasted or be expected to last 12 months. Most people are then asked to an assessment, by phone, video or in person. Keep a copy of everything you send, and if it is turned down ask for a mandatory reconsideration within a month.

Ring the number on the back of the card, or use the app to freeze it, the moment you notice - the bank pays back unauthorised payments and you are not liable for them if you tell them without unreasonable delay. Then ask for the disputed transactions to be refunded, a new card and a new PIN, and say plainly that you did not make the payments and did not give anyone your details. Change the password on the email account the card is registered to, and report it to Action Fraud; if the bank refuses, the free Financial Ombudsman takes it after eight weeks.

Ring the number on the machine or your bank straight away and tell them the machine kept the card: the bank cancels it and sends a new one, usually within a week. If the machine took the card but did not give the cash, say that too, because the account often still shows the withdrawal and the bank has to correct it.

Ring the surgeries near your new address and ask if their list is open: most take people from their own area, and a practice can say no if you live outside it, so try the next one rather than arguing. Take photo ID and something with the new address to the first appointment. If you are on regular medicine, ask for the repeat prescription to be set up that week, and tell them you have just moved so the old notes are asked for.

Ring the takeaway itself rather than tapping at the app: the restaurant can remake it or refund you in a minute. If they will not, use the missing-item report in the app the same day, with a photo of what did arrive, and dispute that amount on the card as a chargeback if the refund does not come. You do not pay for food you never got, and a driver who never came is the app's problem, not yours.

Ring the vet now, before any symptoms: some garden mushrooms are poisonous to dogs and cats, a few of them deadly, and the dangerous ones look much like the harmless ones. Take a photo of where it was growing and whatever is left of it in a paper bag or a bit of damp kitchen roll, so the vet can identify it, and do not make him sick yourself. If he is already drooling, being sick, shaky or wobbly, say that on the phone, because it makes it urgent.

Ring the vet now for pills, medicine, a battery or a coin, and for anything sharp, a sock or a toy: batteries burn through in hours and some pills are dangerous in one tablet. Don't pull a stick or bone out yourself and don't make him sick unless the vet says so. Signs that it's stuck are retching, drooling, a hard swollen belly, or trying to be sick with nothing coming up — that last one is an emergency.

Ring the vet today if it has been more than 24 hours, and straight away for a puppy under six months, or if there is vomiting, diarrhoea or he seems dull. A dog that refuses food is usually feeling sick or in pain rather than being fussy; if he is bright and drinking, take the bowl away after 20 minutes and offer it again next meal. Meanwhile try warm chicken and rice by hand, and check his mouth and teeth for something stuck.

Ring the water company and ask for the bill to be checked against your meter reading, because an estimated bill built on last summer's hosepipe is the usual cause: read the meter yourself and give them the number. If the meter is turning with all the taps off you have a leak, and most companies cut the bill for a hidden leak once, so ask about their leakage allowance; if it stalls, the Consumer Council for Water is free.

Ring the GP surgery and say you have had a positive test: the booking-in appointment is usually between 8 and 10 weeks, and they will sort the midwife, the scans and the bloods. Start 400 micrograms of folic acid and 10 micrograms of vitamin D every day, and stop alcohol - most of what you eat is still fine, and the list of what is not is short. If the line was faint or early, test again in three days. A negative test with no period in three days is worth testing again; a positive one with pain or bleeding is a call to the GP or 111 rather than something to sit on.

Ring the airline as soon as you know: a cheap fare is usually changeable for a fee plus any difference in fare, and often not refundable at all, so ask before you cancel. Flexible fares cost more on the day but pay for themselves once plans move. If the reason is illness or a bereavement, check your travel insurance before you ring.

Ring the bank on the number on the back of another card or in the app and ask them to block the card the machine kept and post a new one, which takes a few working days: nothing can be spent on it once it is blocked, and the money in the account is untouched. If the atm is in a branch wall and the branch is open, staff can open the machine and hand the card back the same day, so ask. Tell them if the machine showed a balance or took money without paying out, because that is refunded once they check it, and never let a stranger help you get the card out or give them your pin.

Ring the bank's own number - the one on your card, the statement or the app, never a number from a text or a call you did not make - and ask one question: which team froze it and why. It is usually a fraud review, an unusual payment, or an ID and address check, and a branch can clear an ID check the same day with your passport or driving licence and a bill. Ask what will still go through and which direct debits will bounce, and tell them if rent or a bill is due. Ask for the reason and a timescale in writing; if it is still frozen after eight weeks the free Financial Ombudsman takes it.

Ring the booking site or the hotel's own number straight away, then ask in this order: a comparable room nearby at their cost including the taxi, or a full refund for the night plus what you pay for the replacement. Walking a guest to another hotel is standard practice, so say the word "walk" and ask them to confirm it in writing before you leave the desk.

Ring the council tax line and ask for it in writing. Most of these letters are a payment to the wrong reference, a discount never applied, or a bill for a name or date that has changed. Ask for a breakdown instalment by instalment and check it against your bank. If you now live alone, ask for the 25% discount backdated; if the bill is right, ask to spread the arrears.

Ring the council tax line before the next payment date and ask for an affordable payment plan: most councils will spread the arrears over the rest of the year, and an arrangement made before a summons is far cheaper than one made after it. Ask for a full breakdown of the bill and for Council Tax Reduction if your income is low. If it has already gone to a summons or a liability order, do not ignore it: contact the council and the court, ask for a means hearing, and get free advice from Citizens Advice. Once a liability order is made the council can ask for an attachment of earnings or deductions from benefits, but the court has to leave you enough to live on.

Ring the courier or use their app as soon as you spot it: most let you correct the address or email until the parcel is out for delivery, and a redelivery to a neighbour or a pickup point is usually free. Keep the tracking number to hand, and tell the shop you bought from if the tracking shows it delivered.

Ring the Child Benefit Office rather than assume it is gone: payments stop when a child turns 16 unless they stay in approved education or training, when a review form from HMRC goes back unanswered, or when the address or the person claiming is out of date. Look for a review or renewal letter first, return it, and ask for it to be backdated - it is usually restored from the date it stopped. If they say no, ask for the decision in writing and appeal within a month.

Ring them or use their own online booking rather than a message, and take a weekday morning or the start of the week if you can: those are the quiet slots and the ones they can move. Say what you want and roughly how long for - a trim or a colour, a massage, a set of nails - and ask the price before they start. A barber will usually take a walk-in on a weekday afternoon.

Ring them and ask them to send the confirmation while you are on the phone: a booking is only held once they have said yes in writing, with the date, the time and a reference. If nothing has come back, ring rather than email, and check the spam folder first - most confirmations arrive within a few minutes of the call.

Ring your GP or the early pregnancy unit today for any bleeding in pregnancy - not because the worst is likely, but because they can check you and it is the same day's job. Bleeding is common in early pregnancy and most people who have it go on to have a healthy baby. Ring 999 or 911 if it is heavy with clots, the pain is bad or on one side, you feel dizzy or faint, or you have pain at the tip of a shoulder - that needs looking at at once.

Ring your bank the same day and ask them to recall it: a faster payment cannot be pulled back, so your bank has to ask the receiving bank, which needs the recipient's permission. Ask them to write to the other bank anyway and to give you their details for a claim, and if the recipient will not hand it back, a money claim online is the route with the refusal in writing. Never pay anyone who offers to get it back: that is the recovery scam.

Ring your bank's fraud line the same day and say the payment was a scam: since October 2024 UK banks have to refund authorised push-payment fraud up to £85,000, with £100 off the top, and speed is what decides these claims. Report it to Action Fraud too, give the police the reference, and keep every message from the seller.

Ring your council's waste line or use the form on their website: a broken or stolen bin is usually replaced free, and a missing or wrong-sized one costs about £20 to £50. Say which bin it is, your address and what happened; a replacement normally turns up in a couple of weeks. Don't buy and use your own unless they tell you that you can, because most rounds will not empty an unofficial bin.

Ring 111 or your GP today and say your child is breathing fast or working to breathe. Fast breathing - over 40 breaths a minute in a baby, 30 in a toddler - sucking in under the ribs, flaring nostrils, grunting or a new wheeze all need a same-day check, because small children tire quickly. Ring 999 if they go blue, limp, or cannot get a breath.

Ring 111 for the out-of-hours dental service: they can book you an urgent appointment at a surgery that is open, and they can prescribe antibiotics if the tooth is infected. Until then, take ibuprofen or paracetamol as the packet says, keep the mouth clean, and do not put aspirin next to the gum. Swelling that closes the eye, a fever or trouble swallowing is a hospital job, so ring 999 or go to A&E.

Ring adult social care at the council first: most run a telecare service for about £3 a week, and a falls assessment can bring the price down or make it free. Ask for that assessment as well, because grab rails by the stairs, a key safe for the ambulance crew and a strength and balance class prevent more falls than an alarm catches. The pendant only helps if it is worn, day and night, and if someone rings back when it goes off, so check who answers before you choose one.

Ring and ask for the retentions or cancellations team, because that is the line allowed to move a price: say "I've had a cheaper quote at £X - what can you do?" Have that quote in front of you, be ready to say you will switch, and ask what the new price ties you into. Write down the date, the name of the person and what they promised, and check the first bill; if you are still in contract there may be an exit fee, and it is only worth paying if the saving beats it.

Ring a dentist within a day or two: a lost or broken filling leaves the tooth tender and it can chip further, and the sooner it is replaced the simpler and cheaper it usually is. Keep the gap clean with gentle brushing, chew on the other side, skip very hot, cold or sticky food, and take paracetamol or ibuprofen if it aches. A pharmacy sells a temporary filling kit to cover it for a few days. Go straight in if the tooth is badly broken or bleeding, or your face swells.

Ring if you want it sorted this week, and write if you need a record. A call gets an answer the same day and you can ask a second question; a letter or an email is what you point to later if nothing happens. The easiest is both: ring, then send two lines saying what was agreed and by when, and keep a copy.

Ringworm is a fungus, not a worm: an itchy red ring of scaly skin that clears in the middle. A pharmacy antifungal cream - clotrimazole or terbinafine - twice a day does it, and keep using it for a week after the ring has gone or it comes back. Keep the skin dry, do not share towels, and wash bedding and socks hot. See a GP if it is on the scalp or the nails, if it is spreading, or if it is no better after two weeks.

Rinse quinoa well, simmer it in twice its volume of salted water for 15 minutes, then drain and let it steam with the lid on for 5. Rinsing takes off the bitter coating; the grains are done when the little tails pop out.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, cook it 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water with the lid on, and leave it alone: 12 minutes on a low simmer, then 10 minutes off the heat. Stirring while it cooks is what makes rice gluey.

Rinse them under cold water and leave them an hour in salty water so they spit out the sand, then steam or grill them for about four minutes, until the shells open. They have no beard to pull like a mussel, and any that will not open go in the bin. Garlic, chilli, lemon and parsley is all they need.

Rinse under cold running water and rub the surface between your hands - a colander under the tap and a shake does most of it, a salad wants its leaves separated and dried in a tea towel, and grapes want the bunch broken up so the water reaches all of them. Soap and washing-up liquid are not for food, and a sealed bag marked ready to eat is already washed.

Rinse aid and salt first: without rinse aid the water clings in drops, so fill the rinse-aid compartment and set it to 4 or 5, and top up the salt. Use the hottest programme you have and open the door an inch when it finishes so the steam escapes; plastic always dries worse than china. If the load is still soaked, clean the filter and check the spray arms turn freely.

Rinse it until the water runs clear, use 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water, bring it to a boil, then turn it right down, put the lid on and leave it 10 minutes without stirring. Take it off the heat and let it sit 5 minutes with the lid on, then fork it through from the bottom - that steam is what makes the grains separate.

Rinse it in cold water straight away, never hot, which sets blood in. Rub in a little washing-up liquid or soak it in cold salt water, then wash as normal; dried blood usually comes out after a soak in a biological detergent.

Rinse it in cool water the moment you get out, chlorine or salt and all, and wash it by hand now and then with a little mild soap. Never wring it, never put it in the machine or the dryer, and dry it flat in the shade: heat and wringing are what stretch the elastic and turn the colour.

Road tax is now on the car, not the windscreen, so you can check it at gov.uk's 'check if a vehicle is taxed' page from the number plate. The amount depends on the first registration date, the CO2 figure and the list price, and it can be paid monthly by direct debit. Driving untaxed should mean the car is on a SORN and off the road.

Roald Amundsen's Norwegian team reached the South Pole first, on 14 December 1911, and Robert Scott's British team arrived on 17 January 1912 to find their tent and flag already there; Scott's party died on the way back.

Roaming is your phone using a network abroad instead of your own, and it costs extra unless your plan or your destination is inside a deal. Turning data roaming off before you fly costs nothing and stops the surprise; check your own plan's roaming page rather than the word on the advert.
Roast sausages at 200C (180C fan) for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, or fry them on a medium heat for about 15. Pricking them lets the juice out, so don't.

Roast beef is 50C rare, 55C medium rare, 60C medium and 70C well done inside, read in the thickest part; it climbs about 5C while it rests, so pull it out 5C under what you want and rest it 15 minutes before carving, and at 220C (200C fan) allow 12 minutes per 500g. A steak is a pan question, not a roast one.

Roast 300g of shelled peanuts at 180C (160C fan) for 10 minutes until they smell nutty, then blitz them in a food processor for 3 to 5 minutes, scraping down the sides: first it is crumbs, then a ball, then suddenly a smooth butter. Add a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of honey, and a spoon of oil if you want it looser. It keeps a month in a jar.

Roast meat keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge, sliced and covered, and freezes for 2 to 3 months. Rare beef is at the shorter end: 3 days. Reheat it once in gravy so it does not dry out, and eat the rest cold.
Robert Downey Jr plays Tony Stark: Iron Man (2008) through Avengers: Endgame (2019). He started the Marvel film run and was in nine of them.

Robert Pattinson plays Batman in The Batman (2022). Before him: Christian Bale in the Dark Knight trilogy (2005-2012), Ben Affleck in the two Justice League-era films, and Michael Keaton in 1989 and 1992.

Robert Walpole is counted as the first British prime minister: he ran the government from 1721 to 1742 and was called first lord of the treasury rather than prime minister, which was meant as an insult at the time.

Roll the first finger slightly onto its bony outer edge rather than flat on the pad, keep the thumb low behind the neck and pull the elbow in towards your body - the pressure comes from the arm, not from squeezing. Start at the fifth fret where the strings are easier, get one clean barre there, then walk the same shape down a fret at a time; a guitar set up with high action will not let you barre cleanly, so that is the next thing to fix.

Roll a frozen bottle of water under the arch for ten minutes and stretch the calf against a wall twice a day: most foot ache is the calf pulling on the arch, not the foot itself. Shoes with a firm sole and room in the toe help more than cushions, and if it is worst first thing in the morning, ask a podiatrist about plantar fasciitis.

Roll a lint roller or a strip of sticky tape over the hard floors and worktops, and vacuum the carpet, then wipe the vacuum head: glitter sticks to everything. A slightly damp cloth gets the last pieces off hands and surfaces.

Roll everything and stand the rolls on end like books on a shelf: a case is a box, and packing flat leaves a third of it empty. Shoes go heel to toe along the spine with socks and chargers inside them, the heavy end goes at the wheels, and whatever you might want out goes on top. In a rucksack the weight sits high and close to your back rather than at the bottom, with the waterproof and a change of clothes at the top. Wear the bulky shoes and the coat on the day.

Roll it off with a lint roller, or wind sticky tape round your hand, sticky side out, and press and lift: that beats any brush on a dark fabric, and a damp rubber glove does the same job. Wash the garment inside out, apart from towels and fleeces, which are what sheds it, and empty the tumble dryer's filter after every load - a full one blows fluff back onto the clothes. New towels shed for their first few washes, so wash them alone until they stop.

Rosacea is a skin condition that flushes and reddens the cheeks, nose and chin, with stinging and sometimes small pus-filled spots, and it comes and goes in flares. Use a mild cleanser, a daily sunscreen (sun is the commonest trigger), and trim the other triggers: alcohol, hot drinks, spicy food, a hot shower, stress. The GP can prescribe a gel - metronidazole, azelaic acid or ivermectin - or a course of antibiotics, which calm it over weeks rather than days. It is not acne and it is not infectious. See the GP if the nose thickens or the eyes are gritty and red, because ocular rosacea is treated too.

Rosemary, thyme and oregano are bought as small plants or grown from softwood cuttings in summer, not from seed: seed is slow and comes up uneven. They want sun, very free drainage - grit in the compost, or a gravel mulch - and far less water than basil; a woody herb in wet soil rots at the base.

Roses flower from June into the first frosts: a first flush in June, then waves if you keep deadheading. Cut each spent flower back to a strong shoot rather than just taking the petals, and a feed after the first flush is what brings the second one on.

Rotate it head to foot every three months, and only flip it if the label or the shop says it is two-sided: most modern mattresses have their comfort layer on top and are made never to be turned over. A two-sided one gets flipped and rotated on the same schedule; a pillow-top or memory-foam one is only rotated, because flipping puts the soft layer underneath.

Rotate it head to foot every three months, and put a 6mm plywood board over the slats if they bow: a dip is nearly always the base or the foam settling, not the springs going. Lay a broom handle across the width - a gap of more than about 2cm under your hip is a real dip, and past seven or eight years a new mattress is the cheaper answer. A topper hides a dip for a year, it does not fix it.
Rough night, then. Coffee only covers so much — get twenty minutes flat on your back this afternoon if you can, and keep the evening quiet.

Rough puff, which is the home version: 250g plain flour, 250g of butter still cold from the fridge cut into 1cm cubes, a pinch of salt, and about 120ml of iced water. Bring it to a dough with the butter still in visible lumps, rest it 20 minutes, then roll it out to a long rectangle, fold the top third down and the bottom third over it, and turn it a quarter turn. Do that four times, resting it in the fridge for 20 minutes if it starts to feel soft, and chill it 30 minutes before it goes in the oven. Cold butter and cold hands are what make it rise: if the butter melts into the flour it bakes flat and tough. Bake at 220C. Real puff, with a flattened block of butter folded inside, is worth buying for a special occasion; filo is always worth buying.

Roughly: 7kg for one or two people, 8kg for three, 9kg for four and 10 to 12kg if you wash duvets and bedding in it. The figure is the dry weight of a full load, so a 9kg drum is not gentler, it just holds more; a bigger one costs more to run per wash but you run it less often. Measure the gap and the doorway first, because depth is what usually rules a machine out, and match the dryer to the washer or slightly bigger than it.
Roughly: a dog 10 to 13 years, a cat 12 to 15, a rabbit 8 to 12, a guinea pig 5 to 7, a hamster 2 to 3, a budgie 8 to 12, and a goldfish 10 or more in a proper tank. Which animal is it?

Round brown or black spots on the leaves are usually a fungus getting in where the leaf stayed wet. Take off the worst leaves and stop misting and splashing the leaves; water the compost instead, in the morning, and give the plant more air. If the spots are soft, spreading fast, or there is a smell, take it out of the room - rot in a stem does not come back.

D-Day was 6 June 1944, when about 156,000 Allied troops landed on five beaches in Normandy in northern France: Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword. It opened the western front against Germany and by the end of August Paris was free.

Royal icing sets hard: keep it in an airtight tub at room temperature for about 2 weeks, or freeze it for up to 3 months, and cover the surface with cling film straight away because it starts to crust as soon as it meets the air. Sugar paste keeps 2 to 3 weeks in a sealed bag, and a drop of water is what revives a dry one. Neither belongs in the fridge - the damp makes both go sticky.

Rub the rod with a candle end or furniture wax, or spray it with silicone, and the rings will run again: the squeak is the rod and the ring, not the fabric. Plastic gliders go chalky and grip after a few years, so replace them, and check the brackets are not sagging in the middle, which pinches the two curtains against each other. A track gets the same treatment plus a vacuum along the slot, because fluff in the runners does most of the sticking.

Rub the tin with butter or a flavourless oil, then cut a circle of baking parchment for the base - a square folded into quarters and trimmed to the corner is the quick way - and grease that too. For muffins and small tins, grease every cup and dust with flour, or use paper cases. Run a thin knife round the edge the moment it comes out and leave the cake in the tin for 10 minutes before turning it out.
Rub the white marks off with a pair of clean tights or a damp sponge. Let the deodorant dry fully before dressing, or switch to a stick or a clear gel and the marks mostly stop.

Rub the inside of the tin all over with butter or a little oil, then dust it with flour and tip the extra out, or cut a circle of baking parchment for the base: either is enough for a sponge, and both together never hurt. For a fruit cake or a big loaf, line the sides with a strip of paper too, and let the cake cool 10 minutes in the tin before you turn it out. A pastry case wants only a thin smear of butter and no flour, or the base goes soggy.

Rub them off with your fingers or a strong jet of water, then spray with soapy water - a teaspoon of washing-up liquid in a litre, sprayed under the leaves in the evening - and repeat every three days for a fortnight, because the eggs keep hatching. Check for ants running up the stem: they farm the aphids and keep them there, so a sticky band round the pot stops the supply line. Ladybirds and hoverflies do the rest if you leave the flowers they feed on. On broad beans, pinch out the top 10cm once the flowers set, which is where blackfly gather.

Rub your hands on something stainless steel under cold running water, like the tap or a spoon, and the smell goes; salt, lemon juice or coffee grounds work too. The sulphur compounds bind to the metal instead of your skin.

Rub a thin coat of food-safe mineral oil into both faces and the edges once a month, and more often in a dry kitchen: that is all seasoning a board is, and olive or vegetable oil go rancid in the wood, so use mineral oil or a board wax. A board that has warped wants the same oil after a drink, because one face has taken on water that the other did not: damp both faces, lay it flat on the worktop with a heavy pan across it for a few days, then wash it, stand it up to dry and oil it. A board that has split down the grain cannot be cleaned safely enough for food afterwards, so sand the crack out flat or replace it, and never soak a board or put it in the dishwasher.

Rub a thin film of butter or flavourless oil all round the inside with a piece of kitchen paper. A cake tin also wants a dusting of flour, tapped round and the extra tipped out, or a lining of baking parchment on the base; a pan or a roasting tin wants only the oil, wiped on while it is cold.

Rub a candle, a dry bar of soap or a little beeswax along the wooden runners or the plastic slides, and never oil or grease - those hold the dust that makes it worse. If it rattles or grinds, tighten the runner screws at the back, one turn past finger-tight. A drawer that sticks only at the end is usually the side swelling in damp weather, so sand the top edge of the drawer side lightly and it stops catching.

Rub a drop of washing-up liquid or shaving foam over the glass and buff it off with a dry cloth: the thin film breaks the water into a sheet instead of droplets, and it lasts a week or two. The same trick works on a car mirror and the inside of a shower screen. Squeegeeing is what stops the water marks in the meantime.

Rub a light scratch on a wooden floor with a walnut (really), or use a wax repair stick in a matching colour for deeper ones. On laminate, a scratch repair pen hides it, but only replacing the board fixes a deep gouge.

Rub a little washing-up liquid or a paste of bicarbonate of soda into the collar and leave it 15 minutes before washing. Wash shirts inside out at the hottest temperature the label allows, and treat the collar each time: once it's grey, heat makes it set.

Rub it with an oil-based cleanser, baby oil or a little cooking oil, then wash with soap; alcohol hand gel or nail polish remover works on ink that's already dry. It wears off in a day or two anyway, and it isn't harmful on ordinary skin.

Rubbing two materials together can pull electrons from one to the other, leaving a charge that builds up on a surface. When you touch something, the charge jumps across as a small spark, which you feel as a shock.

Rugby offside is about where you stand relative to the ball, not the goal line: stay behind the ball, or behind the last foot of the ruck or maul, until it is played away, and come back onside before you get involved. In open play, a team-mate's kick puts you offside until you are put onside by a chase or a pass — and standing in front of the kicker and going for the ball is the one that gives away a penalty.

Rugby league is 13 a side over two 40-minute halves, and the side with the ball gets six tackles to make progress before it goes to the other team. A try is four points and a penalty two, where union scores five and three - that is the quickest way to tell the two codes apart.

Run tall and quiet: a slight lean from the ankles, feet landing under your hips rather than out in front, and a quicker, shorter stride - about 170 to 180 steps a minute. Think light and quick, not long. Finish an easy run with 4 x 30 seconds of fast relaxed strides, and film yourself side-on once: overstriding is the fault nearly everyone has.

Run the tank dry, or fill it right up with a fuel stabiliser in it - a half-full tank of last autumn's petrol is what makes a spring start-up a repair. Then change the oil while the engine is still warm so the dirt comes out with it, scrape the grass from under the deck and oil the blade. Keep it in a dry shed or a garage on a shelf or a pallet rather than on a concrete floor, which holds damp and rusts the deck from underneath, and take the battery off and charge it once a month if it has one.

Run the HDMI cable from the laptop to the projector, then pick the right input on the projector's own menu. On Windows press Windows key + P and choose Duplicate (same picture on both) or Extend (a second desktop); on a Mac, System Settings > Displays > Arrange. If the laptop screen goes black instead, press Windows key + P again, because the picture is going nowhere.

Run the extractor while you shower and for twenty minutes after, or open a window, and keep the door shut so the wet air stays in one room. Wipe the walls down, dry washing outside rather than over a radiator, and keep the heating on low: warm air holds the water, a cold bathroom drops it on the walls. If it carries on, the fan is under-powered or the duct is blocked.

Run the maker's descaling cycle with its own descaler, or citric acid at about 20g to a litre of warm water, then flush two full tanks of clean water through before you drink from it again. A bean-to-cup machine usually prompts you and takes 20 to 30 minutes; a filter machine is a jug job, so run the solution through and rinse twice. Vinegar works at a pinch but leaves a taste and hardens some seals.

Run cold water through the back of the stain, rub in a little washing-up liquid or stain remover and leave it 15 minutes, then wash at the hottest the label allows. Turmeric stains fade further in sunlight if you hang the washed item outside for a few hours.

Run a descaler through an empty drum on the hottest cycle: a 500g bag of citric acid from a hardware shop, or a washing-machine descaler, straight into the drum rather than the drawer, at 60C or 90C, then a rinse cycle with nothing in it. In a hard water area that is every three months; where the water is soft, once a year is enough. White flakes on dark washing and a machine that takes longer to heat are the two signs it is due, and a filter full of grit after the cycle is normal. Skip vinegar: it is hard on the rubber and the seals, and citric acid does the job better.
