Take an aisle seat if you get up, want to stretch a leg out, or are tall; a window if you want to sleep against the wall and not be climbed over. The middle seat is the one to avoid. An exit row buys legroom but no bag under the seat in front.

Take away the food and the easy way in: bins with clipped lids, no pet food or bird food left out overnight, and no fallen fruit under the tree. A 2m fence is not enough on its own, because a fox can clear it or dig under it, so fit a roller bar on top or a strip of paving on the ground line. Chilli powder and commercial repellents fade in the rain and have to be renewed; a dog is the only deterrent that works every night.

Take a mouthful of water first, put the tablet on your tongue, then drink from a bottle or through a straw - and tip your head the right way: a tablet is denser than water so it sinks, so tilt your head back, while a capsule floats, so tip your chin down. Swallowing with a mouthful of yoghurt or a soft banana hides the shape. If it is still hard, ask the pharmacist for a liquid, a dispersible or a smaller tablet, but never crush or split one that says not to - some are slow release.

Take a mouthful of water first, put the tablet further back on your tongue than feels natural and swallow with your chin tipped slightly down, which opens the throat. If it is a plain tablet the pharmacist can usually give the same medicine as a smaller one or a liquid, so ask rather than cutting a slow-release one.

Take a sliver off at a time and stop at the pink centre, the quick: hold a torch under the nail and it shows as a darker oval to aim short of. Cut straight across rather than at an angle, keep the treats coming, and if he hates it do one nail a day. If you do cut too far, press kitchen roll or a pinch of flour on it for a couple of minutes and it stops; walks on pavement wear them down in between.

Take a warm mid layer and a waterproof shell, plus long sleeves rather than vests - even in June the evenings drop to about 8C. Add a hat and gloves if you are going high or out on the water, and midge repellent for anywhere damp and windless in high summer.

Take a counter offer only if it fixes the reason you looked, in writing, with a date: more money at the same job answers the money question and nothing else, and most people who accept one have left within a year anyway. Ask what changes in the next six months and who else knows about it, because an off-cycle rise that only you and your manager know about puts a target on your back. If the reason was the work or the manager, the counter offer is a kindness, not a fix - thank them, keep the new start date, and leave on good terms.

Take goggles, a towel, a swimming costume (not shorts for most pools), a padlock for the locker and £1 coins or a card for it. Most pools want a shower before you get in, and many have a fast lane and a slow lane — start in the slow one.

Take in three photos of cuts on hair like yours - same thickness and wave, not a different length - and ask for the nearest thing to one of them, because a photo says more than any name for a cut. Then say what you hate about it now: too flat on top, too heavy at the sides, frizzy ends. Ask for a dry cut if yours is curly, and if it is a big change have it two weeks before the interview or the wedding, not the day before, so it has time to settle.

Take it off the heat and let it cool where nobody will grab it - and do not put cold water in it while it is hot, because a hot dry pan can warp or crack and the steam spits. Once it has cooled, look at the base: a rainbow tint or a blue-black patch is the metal heat-tinted, which is fine and does not affect the cooking, while food stuck on lifts in a soak of hot water and a spoon of bicarbonate of soda. A pan that boiled dry with nothing in it usually only needs a wash, and one with milk or sugar in it wants the soak.

Take it plainly and say so: "Thanks for saying that - it means a lot." Then, if something is still needed, name one thing in a sentence ("a text next time you are running late would help") and leave it there. You do not have to forgive on the spot; accepting the apology is enough for today.

Take it back to the shop with the packet and the receipt and ask for the money back, and keep the packet: selling food past its use-by date is an offence, so if the shop is not bothered, report it to the council's environmental health team with a photo of the label and the date. A use-by date is about safety, so do not eat it, while a best-before date is only about quality: that one is a refund and nothing worse.

Take it down on Twelfth Night, 5 January, which is twelve days after Christmas - 6 January if you count Epiphany itself. A real tree is usually dropping by then anyway, and the older superstition about leaving decorations up past that night is not one to lose sleep over.

Take just the clear hook off the end and stop well before the pink quick: hold the paw, press the pad so the claw comes out, and cut straight across the tip. Do one or two claws a day with a treat if she hates it, and keep a scratching post so she wears them down herself.

Take lavender cuttings in late summer, from the soft new growth at the tip and never from the old woody stem: a piece about 10cm long, stripped of its lower leaves, pushed into a pot of gritty compost, and kept damp in a bright but shaded spot. They root in six to eight weeks, and a plastic bag over the pot for the first fortnight keeps them from wilting. Autumn cuttings are ready to plant out the following spring.

Talk to the salesperson, not whoever greets you, and go at the end of the month when the targets are close: get a rival dealer's price for the same car in writing and ask them to beat it. Keep the car itself to about a quarter of your yearly take-home, and settle that price before anyone mentions your part-exchange or a monthly payment.

Talk to them once, at a calm time, and say when it happened and what you need: "this has gone on after 11pm most nights this week, and I'm up at six - can it stop by then?" Name the time and the nights, not the person. If it carries on, keep a short log of dates and times and report it to the council's noise team, who can act on it without you having to confront anyone.

Talk to your head of sixth form first: in the first few weeks a change is usually free, and after that the exam entry deadlines are what decide it - entries are made in the winter, so the sooner the better. Dropping to three is fine for almost every university, but tell UCAS and your firm choice if an offer names four, and check that the subject you keep is not a requirement for the course you want. A fourth A level you are failing helps nobody.

Talk to her once, on her own, and say what you know without asking her to explain: 'I know, and I am not going to pretend I don't.' Then be clear about your own line - that you will not lie for her - and leave the telling to her, because it has to be her that does it. Decide in advance whether you will still be her friend if she does not, and say so plainly rather than nagging her every week.

Talk when you are both calm and ask before you tell: one short, curious talk lands better than a lecture, which teaches them to hide it. The facts that land are the money - a disposable a day is about £1,500 a year - and the nicotine: one vape can hold as much as a pack of cigarettes, so stopping brings real withdrawal. It is far less harmful than smoking, so do not push them back. The NHS stop smoking service helps a teenager who wants to stop.

Talk about the specific things rather than the address: stairs, the bath, the boiler, who would notice if they fell. Fix what is fixable first - a grab rail, a shower stool, a key safe, a pendant alarm, a cleaner - and ask the council for a care needs assessment, which is free and does not commit them to anything. Then let them keep the decisions; moving is a last step, not a first one.

Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

Tap the screen to set the focus and the exposure, then drag the little sun slider down a notch, because night shots are wrecked by one bright light in the frame. Brace the phone on a wall or a table and hold still while Night mode takes its couple of seconds, and turn the flash off: it lights the air rather than the subject. Clean the lens with your sleeve first, since a smeared lens is the commonest cause of bad night photos.

Tap the file in your email or downloads and it opens in the phone's own viewer, where pinching zooms and a tap hides the controls. To keep one to hand, use the Books app on an iPhone or Google Drive's PDF viewer on Android, and turn the phone sideways for a wider page.

Tap each mussel before cooking and bin any that stays open, plus any with a broken shell; after cooking, bin the ones that stayed shut, because an unopened one was dead before it went in. Steam the rest in a covered pan with a splash of wine or water for four to five minutes, and eat them the same day rather than keeping them for tomorrow.

Tap it on a flat worktop, not the rim of the bowl: one firm tap, turn it a quarter and tap again, then pull the halves apart over the bowl with your thumbs and let it drop. The flat tap cracks the shell in a line; a rim tap dents it and pushes shell into the egg. If a piece does go in, lift it out with a wet finger or the edge of a shell half, which the white will not cling to.

Tap it with the handle of a screwdriver: a hollow ring means the adhesive has let go, so the tile has to come off and go back properly rather than be patched. Score the grout round it, ease a thin scraper behind a corner and lift it out, then scrape the old adhesive off both the tile and the wall, spread flexible tile adhesive over the whole back with a notched trowel, press it home with a slight twist and tape it in place overnight before you regrout the joints.

Tax it before you drive it away: with the new keeper slip from the seller's V5C you can tax it at gov.uk in a couple of minutes, and the tax does not transfer from the old keeper. Insurance has to be in place first, and you need the MOT if the car is over three years old. The old keeper gets a refund for the rest of their tax automatically.

Tea has enough caffeine to keep you awake if it's after about 2pm, so switch to a herbal one or a warm drink without caffeine in the evening. A milky drink is fine; it's the caffeine and the late loo trip that cost you sleep.

Teach a 'leave it' with a treat in your closed hand, then on the floor, then on a walk, and reward every time he looks at you instead of the ground: a dog that eats first and is told off after does not learn. Walk him on a head collar or a short lead past the bins, take high-value treats on the route, and feed a bit less at home so the search for food is less urgent. Ring the vet straight away if he swallows something that could block him - a bone, a corn cob, a sock - or if he is retching.

Teach "leave it" with a treat in each hand: say it, show the treat, and reward him the second he looks away, then practise on walks with a boring bit of food before you try it on a chip. Keep him on a short lead past takeaways and bins and feed him before walks so he isn't hungry; if he swallows things that could block him, muzzle training is worth the time, because a sock or a kebab stick means surgery.

Tear off the clean lid and put that in the recycling; the greasy base goes in the general waste, or in the food waste if your council takes that. Cheese and oil soaked into card spoil the load at the sorting plant, so a soaked box is the one thing worth separating.

Tears at bedtime are usually overtiredness or a routine that changes shape from night to night: the same four or five steps in the same order at the same time (bath, milk, teeth, two books, lights low, into bed), starting the wind-down half an hour before, with the last nap not too late for a toddler. Do the same short goodnight every time and leave while they are awake but sleepy; if they cry, go back after a minute, then two, then three, with a quiet 'it's sleep time, I love you' and no light and no play. It is normal for the first three or four nights to be worse before they are better, and see the GP if they also snore, stop breathing, or are exhausted in the daytime.

Teenagers need more sleep than adults, not less: 8 to 10 hours a night from 14 to 17, and 9 to 12 from 6 to 13. Their body clock also shifts late, so an 11pm natural bedtime is biology rather than laziness, and a school start of 8am means lights out by 10:30 with the phone out of the room for the last hour. A weekend lie-in of more than two hours moves the clock further back and makes Monday worse, so a shorter catch-up and a dark room work better.

Teeth that twinge with cold are usually worn enamel or a gumline that has receded, which leaves the softer dentine underneath exposed. Start with a sensitive toothpaste (the ones with stannous fluoride or arginine) and use it as your everyday paste, spitting rather than rinsing afterwards so it stays on the teeth. Brush gently with a soft brush, wait an hour after acidic food or drink before brushing, and ask your dentist about a fluoride varnish or a filling over the exposed patch. Go sooner if the pain lasts more than a few seconds after the cold is gone, or if one tooth aches on its own at night, because that is more than sensitivity.

Tell payroll in writing today, because money paid by mistake can be taken back and, if it is a real overpayment, keeping quiet looks like dishonesty later. Say what you think is wrong and ask for a written breakdown; a genuine overpayment is usually recovered in agreed instalments, and you can ask for a repayment plan you can afford rather than a lump sum. Put the money aside until it is sorted, so it never feels like yours.

Tell the operator in writing as soon as you know, because the cancellation charge is set by how close you are to leaving: most scales lose the deposit weeks out and the whole price in the last week or two, so ask for their scale in writing. If you are ill, travel insurance pays, with a doctor's note and a call before you cancel. Cheaper routes: transfer it to someone else, or move the date for a fee.

Tell the organiser within 28 days of getting home: that's the deadline in the Package Travel Regulations, and claims after it get much harder. Keep the photos, receipts and any emails with the rep, and name the organiser you booked with, not the hotel.

Tell the people coming first, and as early as you can: one line on why, a new date or two in the same message so it is a move rather than a hole, and a fresh invite. Ring the person who would have chaired it rather than emailing a room, and say what happens to the thing the meeting was for. Cancelling your own meeting is cheap early and expensive late.

Tell the person or company what you can pay and when, even if it is £10 a month - a payment plan beats silence, so say it before it snows. Rent, council tax and energy come before credit cards, and a maxed-out card wants the minimum paid on the day every month. A free service like StepChange or National Debtline will write to everyone for you.

Tell the person affected before they find out, with the fix attached: "I got the figures wrong in the report; I have corrected them and sent the revised version to everyone who had the first one. I have added a check so it does not happen again." Say it once, plainly, no long apology, and then answer questions. Nobody remembers the mistake; they remember whether you brought it to them or they found it.

Tell the places that fine you or bill you first: the tax office or council, the bank, your insurer, the driving licence people and your employer's payroll. Then the doctor, dentist, school and any subscriptions. A mail redirect for three months catches what you forgot, and it is cheaper than a missed letter.

Tell the airline desk as soon as you know - the booking is still yours, so they can usually move you to a later flight, and someone can bring the passport to the airport if there is time. If it is at a hotel, ask them to hold it and courier it to you; a photo of it will not get you through security.

Tell the insurer the same day and photograph everything before anything is repaired or thrown away, because a claim reported late or after the fix is the one they refuse. Have the policy number, dates and receipts ready, expect the excess off the payout, and never admit fault to the other side - the insurer handles that. If they refuse or drag it out eight weeks, complain in writing and then take it free to the Financial Ombudsman.

Tell the insurer as soon as you can, before you throw anything away: keep the damaged item, take photos, and photograph anything that proves what it was worth. They send a loss adjuster for anything large, and the first thing they check is whether you said yes to the right cover, so have the receipts or the bank statements ready.

Tell the insurer before you fix or replace anything: most policies want the damage seen first, and repairing early turns a claim into a negotiation. Photograph everything, keep receipts and quotes, and report a theft to the police for a crime number. Ask what the excess is before you go ahead, because a claim smaller than the excess costs you money, and claim on one policy only when two could cover it.

Tell the landlord in writing before the next rent day, and ask the council about a Discretionary Housing Payment and that the Housing Element of Universal Credit is paid straight to them. Shelter (0808 800 4444) is free and will check what you have been served, and an eviction always needs proper notice and a court order.

Tell them once, plainly, that you have heard them and you are going anyway: 'I know you think it is a mistake, and I am still going.' You do not need their agreement, only their being told before anyone else hears it, so they are not left guessing.

Tell them together, in plain words, and make the one thing clear they need to hear: it is not their fault and both of you will keep loving them. Keep the details and any blame between the adults, and let them ask the same questions again over the next weeks; that is how children make sense of it.

Tell them as soon as it is certain, and keep it concrete: which room is theirs, where the school or nursery is, and what stays the same. Let them pack a box of their own things and choose the paint or the posters, because control is what they are missing. Say goodbye to the old place properly on the last day, and expect a wobble a few weeks in, when the novelty wears off and they miss their friends.

Tell them early, in a call rather than a text, and give them the plan instead of only the no: 'We're staying here this year and we'll come up in January.' Say it once, then let them be disappointed without arguing them out of it - 'I know, and this is what we've decided.' Offer one concrete thing (a video call on the day, a visit you both get to look forward to) so the conversation ends on something instead of a silence.

Tell your bank or card company the same day and use the word unauthorised: it has to be refunded in full by the end of the next working day, and the bank can refuse only if it can show you were grossly negligent or handed the money over. Ask for a new card, report it to Action Fraud for a crime reference, and if the bank stalls, complain and the Financial Ombudsman takes it free after eight weeks.

Tell your manager before you apply, in one sentence and without apologising: "I saw the analyst role in the other team and I want to go for it - I wanted you to hear it from me." Then apply through the internal process, because the hiring manager cannot usually offer it to you off the record. Ask what happens to your notice period, your holiday and your start date if you get it, and check the contract for a minimum time in post: six or twelve months is common and it is often waivable with your manager's agreement.

Tell your manager in writing the same day, with the date, the place and what you saw - and put it in the accident book if anyone was hurt, because that record is what counts later. If nothing changes within a week, go to the safety rep or the health and safety person named in your workplace, and after that the enforcing body (the HSE, or the council for a shop, office or warehouse). You can refuse work you believe is a serious and imminent danger, and you are protected from being sacked for raising it - so keep copies of everything you send.

Tell her early and keep it about money, not about the friendship: 'I'd love to be there and I can't do the whole thing this year - the travel and the outfit are beyond me.' Then offer one concrete piece you can do, like a night of the hen do or helping on the morning, so she hears that you want to be involved.
Tell me the word and I'll spell out the sounds syllable by syllable in plain English, with the stressed part in capitals. If it is a name, I'll say it the way the person would.

Tell me what the ticket is for and I will be exact, because the rules differ: a train is a refund less a small admin fee, a flight follows the fare's own rules, and a gig or theatre ticket is the seller's terms. What is the same everywhere is that if the company cancels on you, you are owed your money back.

Ten minutes a night, the same time, with them reading out loud to you: stop at the first hard word, sound it out together, and let them finish the sentence. Read the same short book twice, because the second read is where the confidence comes from, and keep a book in the car or bag for dead time. Ask one question about the story afterwards rather than testing words.

Ten minutes first: tyres at the right pressure with 1.6mm of tread across the middle three quarters, every light working including the number plate lamp, wipers clearing, screenwash topped up and the horn sounding. Clear the warning lights off the dash, empty the boot of anything a tester would have to move, and take the V5C or the reference the centre has on file.

Ten minutes is plenty: a jog to get warm, then leg swings, side-steps, lunges and a few short sprints, and finish with the ball or the equipment so the last thing you do looks like the game. Save the long stretches for afterwards.

Ten or fifteen minutes of running on after the light goes off is the timer doing its job, and it is what keeps the damp out. A fan that never stops has an overrun set too long, a stuck timer, or a humidistat turned up too high: take the cover off and look for the overrun screw or a dial inside, set the overrun to about fifteen minutes, and turn the humidistat down to around 60% - if neither is there, or it will not change, the module is a swap, around £25 to £60. A fan that runs only when nobody is in the room, or one that is still going after the isolator is off, is a wiring job.

Ten percent is the easy part: move the decimal point one place, so a £46 bill is £4.60, and half of that again is five percent, so twelve and a half is £5.75. Check the bill for a service charge first, because that is the tip and you add nothing on top.

Ten days is the rule: the deposit has to come back within ten days of the day you and the landlord agree the amount, and interest can come with it. If you have not agreed, the landlord has to return the undisputed part within those ten days and put in a claim for the rest, and a disputed amount goes to the protection scheme, whose free dispute service usually decides within 28 days. So ask the scheme which one holds your money, and chase the agent in writing, because the deadline is counted from the agreement and not from the day you moved out.

Tennis elbow is the tendon on the outside of the elbow overworked by gripping, lifting and typing, so the outside of the elbow aches and the grip weakens; golfer's elbow is the same on the inside. It is not a wait-and-rest injury: rest it from the thing that caused it, but keep using the arm gently, and do the eccentric exercise - a light weight or a tin, wrist slowly down and lift back with the other hand, three sets of fifteen, most days. A brace from a pharmacy helps while it settles, which takes weeks to a few months. See the GP or a physio if it is no better after six weeks, and the same day if there was a bang or the hand is numb, because that is not a tendon.

Tent, sleeping bags and mats for everyone, a torch each so nobody is in the dark alone, and one full change of clothes per child per day plus two spare sets: that is what wet weather costs. Add wellies and a waterproof, wipes and nappy bags, a sun hat and cream, snacks and a water bottle each, their own pillow or blanket, Calpol and plasters, and a bag for wet things. Pitch near the toilets, take a mallet, and put the tent up at home once before you go.

Test the broadband on something else in the house: if a laptop on a cable is fine, it is the wifi, so move the router off the floor and out of a cupboard and use 5GHz for the TV. If everything buffers, it is the connection - check the speed on the router's own app at the time it happens, because slow evenings are usually the provider, and a call with those numbers gets a fault raised.

Test it on the money before anything else: work out what you need to live on for a year, add about a third for tax, your own kit and quiet weeks, and check you have one client who will pay it. Most people who last had six months of savings and a signed first job before they left. Start as a sole trader - it is free to register with HMRC, and a limited company can wait until the work is steady.

Test it once before you decide anything: ask one plain question about their week, then leave a gap and see whether it comes back to you. If it never does, say it lightly and specifically - 'I'd love it if you asked how the job hunt is going' - because most people who only talk about themselves are not being cruel, they are just bad at the turn. Then put your weight where it comes back: keep this one for the good times and let the heavy weeks go to the friends who ask.

Test it with a cable into the router and keep the numbers: the speed at sign-up is a guaranteed minimum, and under Ofcom's code the provider has 30 days to fix it once you report it falling short on three days running. Send those readings in writing as a complaint, and if it is not fixed you can leave without a penalty and claim back the shortfall. Unresolved after 8 weeks, the Communications Ombudsman is free.

Text the same evening or the next morning. There is no waiting rule worth playing, and a day of silence reads as disinterest rather than mystery. Say something specific - 'still thinking about that story about the ferry' - and end with a question or a plan, so it is easy to answer in one line. If nothing comes back, one follow-up after a few days is fine and then leave it: no reply is a reply.

Thank the host, mean it, and go: "It's been lovely - I'm going to head off, thank you so much." Say your goodbyes to the host and the one or two people you actually spent the evening with, not the whole room, and have your reason ready in one line ("early start tomorrow") because the second question is always why. Leaving at the natural lull is easier than the big goodbye, and nobody minds nearly as much as the leaving feels like it will.

That needs A&E today, not next week: a swollen or hard testicle is checked the same day, and say when it started and that it is one side - if the pain came on suddenly it is the twisted kind, which has only a few hours before it is lost. Ring 999 or 911 if the pain is severe, you are being sick, or the scrotum has changed colour.

That needs a vet today, not an appointment next week: a dog who drags a back leg, knuckles over on a paw or suddenly cannot use his back end usually has a slipped disc, and the sooner it is seen the better the chance he walks again. Carry him - a towel under the belly if he is heavy - keep him still and warm, and ring the vet on the way rather than waiting at home to see if it improves. Do not give him anything from the medicine cupboard: ibuprofen and paracetamol are both poisonous to dogs. If it came on after a jump, a fall or a long walk, say so when you ring.

That needs 999 or 911 now, and say someone has been shot. Press hard on the wound with a cloth, add more cloths rather than lifting the one you have, and don't move them unless they are still in danger where they are.

That rub is the fabric against itself, so nothing stops it completely, but three things slow it down a lot: wash them less (once every four or five wears, cold, inside out), skip the tumble dryer because heat weakens the cotton, and put on a couple of kilos' worth of a looser fit - fabric that does not meet does not rub. When it goes, patch it from the inside with an iron-on denim patch before the hole reaches the seam: a patch costs a few pounds and a repairer charges about ten to put one in properly.

That stings, and it is usually about the case rather than the person - so get the reason in writing: what the role needs that they have not seen from you yet, and when it is reviewed again. Do one of those things where people can watch - run the project, cover the report, train the new starter - because a promotion is decided on evidence someone else can point at. If the answer is that there is no role to give you, ask what one would look like and whether it is funded, and put your own date on the decision. Twice with no reason is the company answering you.

That white or grey fuzz on the compost is a fungus eating dead plant matter, and it is harmless to the plant: scrape the top centimetre off, water less and let the surface dry between waterings, and give the room some air. It only appears where the compost stays warm and wet.
That would bother me too. Tell me what it does and I'll work out the next step with you.

That ache a day or two after new or harder exercise is delayed-onset muscle soreness, not damage: it is the muscle repairing itself and it peaks around 48 hours and eases within four days. Keep moving gently, drink water and sleep, and start lighter next time; see someone if one spot is sharp, swollen or bruised, or if your urine goes cola-coloured.

That ache a day or two after new exercise is normal and it is not damage: it is the muscle repairing itself after work it is not used to. Keep moving gently - a walk, an easy swim - rather than resting completely, drink water, and expect it to be worst about 48 hours in and gone within four days. Next time start with less weight or fewer repeats than you think you can do.

That ache a day or two after a new or harder run is normal and it eases faster if you keep moving: a walk or a very easy jog, plenty of water and a normal night's sleep do more than stretching. Go back to running once the soreness is gone in a normal walk, and add distance more slowly next time.

That bang is the pressure wave when a valve shuts quickly and nothing absorbs it: clip any loose pipe run so it cannot jump, replace a worn tap washer or a tired ball valve in the toilet, and fit a mini shock arrestor close to the appliance that bangs. If the whole house does it, ask the water company to check the pressure, or have a pressure reducing valve fitted after the stop tap.

That cough is usually the airways clearing themselves: the little hairs that sweep mucus out start working again once the smoke stops, so a few weeks of coughing up is normal and a good sign. Do not let it send you back to cigarettes. See a doctor if there is blood, if you are breathless, or if it is still there after a month.

That dip after lunch is your body clock, not laziness or a lack of willpower, and it passes. Eat a lunch with protein and fibre rather than a big plate of white carbs, then get ten minutes of daylight and a short walk at the low point instead of another coffee. Drink water, keep the caffeine to before 2pm so it does not cost you tonight, and if you can, take a 15-minute nap rather than a long one.

That dread is usually about one or two things rather than the whole week, so name the worst bit tonight and plan only for that. If it is one meeting or one person, decide now what you will say; if it is all of it, that is a bigger question than one Monday. Tonight: bag and clothes ready, the two jobs tomorrow starts with written down, and one thing in the day you actually want.

That figure is republished every day and two places rarely quote the same one, because each adds its own margin or terms on top: compare two of them and go with the one whose small print fits what you are actually doing, checking the date printed with the number.

That is nearly always heat: clear the vents and the fan with a can of air, keep it off soft surfaces, and note whether it happens only when it has been on a while or only with a heavy app open - that points at the fan or the thermal paste rather than the battery. If it goes off with no warning and no heat, look up the crash in Event Viewer (Windows) or Console (Mac) and check the battery health, because a worn battery cannot hold a heavy load and switches the machine off.

That is normal, especially in the first few days or when something new has arrived: let her hide and do not pull her out. Keep her in one quiet room with food, water and the litter tray close by, sit on the floor and talk or read aloud for ten minutes at a time so she gets used to you, then let her come to you. She should be eating, drinking and using the tray within 24 hours; after three or four days of hiding, or if she stops eating, ring the vet.

That is normal: the cooling fan runs on for a few minutes after you switch off, to pull the heat out of the engine bay, and it can start by itself on a hot day even when the car has been parked a while. Ten or fifteen minutes then silence is fine. If it runs much longer than that, runs every time you stop, or leaves you with a flat battery, the coolant or the fan switch needs looking at.

That is normal and it has a fix: what you re-read fades in a day or two, and what you test yourself on comes back. Same day, look at the topic and cover it and say it out loud; then again after two days, after a week, and after a month. Turn each topic into five questions and keep them on cards, and go through yesterday's cards for two minutes before starting anything new.

That is separation anxiety and it peaks around eight to ten months: they have worked out you still exist when you are gone, and cannot yet trust that you will come back. Play peekaboo and do short practice exits - 'I'm going to the kitchen, back in a minute' - and always come back when you said, so leaving stops being a surprise. It fades on its own over a few months.
That is the short-version opener - go on, then. What happened?

That is the evidence to bring: the years you have been there and the work you took on, put in numbers - the jobs that came off someone else's desk, the people you trained, what changed because of you. Then ask for the specific thing you want - a figure on your pay, or the shifts you are after - rather than a promise.
That is the feeling of knowing a word or name that will not come. It usually arrives a minute later, or when you stop trying. What are you trying to remember?

That is the guest sign-in page doing its job: open a browser and go to any site you have not visited, such as example.com, and the page should appear with a box for the password, room number or your email. If nothing loads, type 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1 in the address bar, or ask the staff for the code; some places ask you to sign in again every hour.

That is the layout, not the keyboard: on Windows press the Windows key and Space to cycle back to English, or click the ENG box by the clock and pick the right one, and turn Num Lock off because it turns the right-hand letters into numbers. If it is only the @ and the quote in the wrong place, the keyboard type is set to United States when you have a United Kingdom one - change it in Settings > Time and language > Language.

That is usually over-stimulation: stroking gets too much for her and the bite is how she says stop. Keep it to the head and cheeks rather than the back and tail, watch for the tail flick and the skin twitch and stop before that, and let her come to you. A sudden change in a cat who used to enjoy it is worth a vet check for pain.

That is usually the proximity sensor working: the screen goes black when the phone is held to your ear so your cheek does not press buttons, and it lights again when you pull it away. If it stays black, take the case or the screen protector off the top edge, where the sensor sits, and give the earpiece slot a wipe with a dry cloth. Restart the phone before you buy anything, and on an iPhone turn off Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Call Audio Routing > Speaker if it is set. A screen that also goes black on its own, not in calls, is the display or the battery - a repair shop job.

That is usually BPPV - tiny crystals loose in the inner ear, so turning the head sets the room spinning for under a minute. It is not a stroke and it is fixable: a GP or a physio does the Epley manoeuvre, which moves the crystals back in one or two visits, and there are steps online to try at home. Sit up slowly and sleep propped on two pillows until it settles. Get seen the same day if it comes with hearing loss, weakness or numbness on one side, double vision, slurred speech, or a sudden bad headache.

That is usually bone and muscle not used to the load: cut back to whatever mileage does not hurt, run on softer ground, and ice the shin for 10 minutes after. New shoes and a shorter stride help more than stretching, and calf raises twice a day build the muscle that takes the strain. A shin with one small spot of sharp pain that hurts to touch, or pain that carries on at rest, needs a GP, since that can be a stress fracture.

That is usually cystitis: drink plenty of water, take paracetamol and pee when you need to rather than holding on, and most cases settle in a day or two. See a GP or pharmacy the same day if it lasts over three days, comes with blood, a fever or back pain, or if you are pregnant, a man or a child. Three or more a year is worth a GP review.

That is what headphones, a mute or a practice room are for, and most of it is cheaper than a row: a headphone amp for an electric guitar, a soundhole cover or a folded cloth in an acoustic, a practice mute for a violin or a brass instrument, and headphones on a digital piano. Pick the hours you would want quiet in yourself - not before nine and not after ten - and tell them once, cheerfully, that you play and when you stop.

That is worth taking seriously, and it is treatable - you are not stuck with it. Tell a GP: they can refer you to an NHS eating disorder service, and in the UK you can also ring Beat's helpline on 0808 801 0677 to talk it through before you decide anything. The thing that helps most at the start is one person who will not panic - a friend, a parent, a nurse - and telling them how often it happens. Try not to start with a diet or a rule about food; eating like this is usually doing a job for a feeling, and a rule gives the feeling nowhere to go. If you feel faint, your heart races, you cannot keep water down or you have not eaten for a day, treat that as urgent and get seen the same day.
That is yours to weigh rather than mine, honestly. What would change your mind?

That is an emergency, so ring your vet now and say the animal will not wake up: most practices have an out-of-hours number for exactly this. Keep him warm and still, do not try to give him anything by mouth, and check he is breathing while you wait. If he has stopped breathing, start chest compressions and keep going until you reach the vet.

That is a phase and it is a common one, not a sign you have got it wrong. Keep putting one new food next to the food they will eat, offer it without comment, and let them leave it; children usually need ten or more tries before they take a new food. Give a children's multivitamin if the list stays that short for months, and never cook a second dinner, because the safe plate is what they will hold out for.

That is a question about the hours you will actually be out, not about the day: under about 10 degrees, yes, and a proper coat with a jumper under it if you will be standing about; between 10 and 18 a jumper and something windproof is enough, and over 18 you carry the coat rather than wear it. Rain decides it more often than cold does, so a waterproof beats a warmer one that lets water through, and the bits that feel it first are the neck, ears, hands and feet.

That is a real cost: an hour each way is about where most people stop being fine with it, and past that it is twenty hours a week, which no pay rise really covers. Put the real numbers down - the season ticket or the fuel, those hours at your hourly rate, and what moving closer would add to the rent - then ask for two days at home before you turn the job down, because that is the part employers say yes to. If you are keeping the journey, make the time yours with a book or a podcast and shift your start half an hour earlier rather than sitting in the worst of it.

That is a real decision, and most people feel two ways at once about it - lighter, and a bit exposed. Two things are much easier now than in a month: check the final payslip for the holiday you have not taken, and ask for a written reference while they still think well of you. What is the plan for the next few weeks - straight into something else, or a bit of a gap first?

The Hundred Years War actually ran 116 years, from 1337 to 1453, between England and France. It was not one continuous war but a series of campaigns, and it ended with England losing everything except Calais.

The Inca empire ran along the Andes from about 1438 to 1533, with its capital at Cusco and perhaps ten million people under it. The Allies won the First World War: Britain, France, Italy, Japan and, from 1917, the United States, against Germany and Austria-Hungary. The fighting stopped on 11 November 1918, and the peace terms were settled at Versailles the following year.

The Moon is about 3,475 km across, a little over a quarter of the Earth's width, and you could fit about 50 Moons inside the Earth. It looks small only because it is about 384,000 km away.

The Moon is grey-brown rock; it looks white because it is lit by direct sunlight against a black sky, and your eyes judge it against that darkness. The bright and dark patches are different rocks, not ice or cloud.

The Moon looks bigger near the horizon because of an illusion in how your brain judges it against the landscape; photograph it and it comes out the same size as when it is high overhead. It also looks dimmer down there, not brighter, because its light is crossing more air.

The Moon makes no light of its own: it reflects sunlight, and at full moon it is opposite the Sun so nearly all of its lit face is turned towards you. Its rock is dark grey, but with no air to dim the light and a black sky around it, it looks brilliant.
The Moon's craters are mostly impact scars from rocks that hit it over billions of years, and with no air or water to erode them they stay. The dark patches are old lava plains, not shadows.

The Anglo-Saxons were the Germanic peoples - Angles, Saxons and Jutes - who settled in Britain from about 450 AD after the Roman legions left, and whose kingdoms, Wessex, Mercia and Northumbria among them, became England. They converted to Christianity from 597, and their rule ended with the Norman conquest in 1066.

The Opium Wars were fought by Britain against Qing China in 1839 to 1842 and again in 1856 to 1860, to keep the opium trade that British merchants ran from India into China after China tried to stop it. Britain won, and the Treaty of Nanking in 1842 handed it Hong Kong and opened five ports.

The Rent a Room scheme makes the first £7,500 a year of rent tax free if you let a furnished room in the home you live in, and there is nothing to declare below that. Take a month's rent as a deposit and give a written licence agreement rather than a tenancy, so it stays easy to end. Tell your home insurer and, if you have one, your mortgage lender or landlord before anyone moves in.

The Roman Empire in the west lasted about 500 years, from 27 BC to 476 AD, and its eastern half, ruled from Constantinople, went on until 1453, so the empire as a whole ran nearly 1,500 years. The republic that came before it had already lasted almost 500 years.

The Roman Empire is usually dated from 27 BC, when Octavian took the name Augustus and became the first emperor, though the republic had already been falling apart for decades. Rome itself was founded, by tradition, in 753 BC, which is why the years before 27 BC are dated from it.

The Silk Road was not a road but a chain of trade routes between China and the Mediterranean, busiest from about 200 BC to 1400 AD. Silk went west and horses, glass and wool went east, and so did religions, paper-making and plagues.

The Spanish Armada was a fleet of about 130 ships sent by Philip II in 1588 to collect an army from the Netherlands and invade England. English fireships broke its formation at Calais, the fleet was driven north by the wind, and storms wrecked much of it on the way home.

The State Pension starts at 66 now, and 67 for anyone reaching that age from 2028. It is not automatic: you should get a letter about two months before you get there, and if it does not come, claim online at gov.uk (Get your State Pension) or ring the Pension Service. You need 10 qualifying National Insurance years to get anything at all and 35 for the full new amount, about £11,500 a year, and a forecast at gov.uk/check-state-pension shows where you stand, because gaps can often be filled with voluntary contributions.

The Sun sends out every colour mixed together, so from space it looks white; through our air the blue is scattered away and what reaches you looks yellow-white. Low in the sky it looks orange because the light crosses even more air on the way in.
The Sun is about 1.4 million km across, roughly 109 Earths side by side, and you could fit about 1.3 million Earths inside it. It looks small only because it is 150 million km away.

The Tudor period ended in 1603, when Elizabeth I died without children and James VI of Scotland took the throne as James I. That joined the crowns of England and Scotland, though the two countries stayed separate until 1707.

The Tudors took the crown when Henry Tudor beat Richard III at Bosworth in 1485, and held it until 1603: Henry VII, Henry VIII, Edward VI, Lady Jane Grey for nine days, Mary I and Elizabeth I. It was the century of the Reformation in England, the Armada, Shakespeare and the first voyages to America, and it ended when Elizabeth died childless and the Stuarts took over.

The UK advice is no more than 70g of red meat a day, and to go easy on processed meat (bacon, ham, sausages) because the cancer link is strongest there. Lean red meat is a good source of iron and zinc, so it is a question of amount and frequency rather than giving it up: two or three meat meals a week and fish or beans the rest.

The UK has no single written constitution and no bill of rights in the American sense; rights come from the Human Rights Act 1998, which wrote the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law, plus ordinary statutes. Under it a court can declare a law incompatible with a Convention right, but only parliament can change the law - which is why a British bill of rights is argued about so often and settled so rarely.

The UVA that tans and ages skin goes straight through glass, so a day by a window or a long drive gives you colour and lines, while the UVB that burns is mostly filtered out. It creeps up on you because you do not feel it getting hot. Glass is not sun protection, so use SPF 30 on the arm and face nearest the window if you sit there for hours, and do not treat a sunbed as a shortcut to the same thing.

The Vikings were Norse traders, farmers and raiders from Denmark, Norway and Sweden who were active from about 793 to 1066. They raided monasteries but also traded, settled and founded towns as far apart as Dublin, Kiev and Newfoundland.

The Warm Home Discount takes £150 off the electricity bill once, between October and March, for people on a low income, and most eligible households get it automatically from their supplier because the government matches the records - check the bill for the credit and ring the supplier if it is missing. Pension Credit or a low income with high energy costs is what qualifies you, and the Winter Fuel Payment and Cold Weather Payment are separate sums paid through the same benefits.

The Winter Fuel Payment is a one-off lump each winter for pensioners who get Pension Credit or another means-tested benefit, paid automatically in November or December, and it is not the Warm Home Discount. The Cold Weather Payment is a separate sum again: £25 for each seven-day spell where the temperature where you live stays at 0C or below, paid within 14 days of the spell.

The Aztec empire fell in 1521, when Spanish forces under Cortes took Tenochtitlan after a three-month siege. Cortes had only a few hundred Spaniards, so what did it was tens of thousands of local allies who resented Aztec tribute, plus smallpox, which killed a large share of the city before the fighting ended.

The Aztecs ruled central Mexico from their city Tenochtitlan, which was built on an island in a lake and was home to 200,000 people by 1500. They farmed the lake on floating plots and paid for everything in tribute and human sacrifice, and Spanish forces under Cortes took the city in 1521.

The G stands for generation: 4G is the fourth, 5G the fifth, and the numbers are a speed-and-latency ladder rather than a brand. 4G took about a tenth of a second to answer and 5G more like a hundredth, which is what makes video calls and live video from a phone work away from wifi; the phone drops to the slower one when the signal is thin, which is why the number in the corner keeps changing.

The amount is set once a year by your council and the bill lands in April: a draft in February, first payment in April. Most of a rise goes on social care and bins, and councils get less government money than they used to. There is no cap on a year's rise. If you live alone, claim the 25% single-person discount; you can also pay over twelve months instead of ten.

The annual foot check is about ten minutes with a practice nurse or a podiatrist: they look at the skin and nails, feel the pulses in your feet and test the feeling in your toes, and ask about your shoes and any sores. It is free and it is how a problem is caught before it becomes an ulcer, so book it if you have not had one in the last year.

The apostrophe goes where the letters were left out: don't for do not, can't for cannot, I'm for I am, won't for will not. That is why won't and can't don't look like the words they shorten - the old forms were woll not and can not.

The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066: William of Normandy beat King Harold, who was killed on the field, and was crowned on Christmas Day. It was the last successful invasion of England, and it replaced the English ruling class with a Norman one.

The Battle of Trafalgar was fought on 21 October 1805, when Nelson's fleet beat the French and Spanish off Cape Trafalgar and destroyed the fleet that was meant to cover an invasion of Britain. The invasion barges at Boulogne never sailed. Nelson was shot on his own deck and died that afternoon, and the victory is the one in the Trafalgar Square column.

The Battle of Waterloo was fought on 18 June 1815 near Brussels, when Wellington's army with Blucher's Prussians beat Napoleon. It ended his rule for good: he abdicated four days later and was exiled to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

The Battle of Britain was fought in the air over southern England in the summer and autumn of 1940: the RAF against the Luftwaffe, with radar and ground control on the British side. Germany could not win the air superiority it needed to invade, so it turned to night bombing, and it was the first battle of the war that Germany lost.

The average band D bill in England is about £2,171 a year for 2025-26. Yours is set by your council and your band, so the exact figure is on your bill. If it is more than you expected, check the band and the 25% single-person discount, and ask to pay over twelve months rather than ten.

The battery has reached the end of its life, so replace it: a laptop that dies the moment the charger comes out cannot hold a load, and no setting will bring it back. Check the health number first - `powercfg /batteryreport` on Windows, System Information > Power on a Mac - because a design capacity under about 70% is a replacement, and a new one is usually £30 to £90 fitted on a Windows laptop and more on an Apple one.

The belt has almost certainly slipped off or snapped: it is a rubber band round the drum and the motor pulley, a few pounds, reached through the back panel with a screwdriver. Turns by hand but not under power? Belt or door switch. Will not turn by hand either? Something is jammed or the bearings have gone, which usually means a new machine.

The Berlin Wall went up on the night of 13 August 1961, when East Germany sealed the border through the city with barbed wire and then concrete, to stop people leaving for the west. It stood for 28 years and came down on 9 November 1989.

The Berlin Wall came down on the night of 9 November 1989, after mass protests across East Germany and a border announcement that was misread as immediate. Crowds crossed and began pulling the wall apart; Germany reunited the following year.
The best of both worlds means getting the good parts of two options at once. What are the two you are choosing between?

The best man looks after the groom and the rings: hold both wedding rings, hand them over at the right moment, keep the groom calm and on time, carry the licence or the paperwork, and look after the gifts and the cards. He organises the stag do and collects for the wedding present from the groom's side, makes sure the groom is dressed, fed and at the ceremony early, and gives the speech after the meal - a short one that thanks the couple on the guests' behalf and embarrasses the groom gently. A maid of honour does the same for the bride: rings and bouquet in hand, dress and phone carried, and the toast if there is one. An usher seats the guests, hands out the orders of service and points people to the car park.

The bill comes out of the estate before anything is shared out, so the money the person left pays for their own funeral. The person who signs the funeral director's form is the one who owes it if the estate cannot cover it, and a bank will often pay the funeral director straight from the account on an invoice. If there is no money at all the council has to arrange and pay for a basic funeral, and the DWP funeral expenses payment covers part of the bill for people on certain benefits.

The black comes back because it lives in the fold of the rubber door seal, so that is the bit to clean: pull the seal open, wipe the fold with a cloth and a little white vinegar or a mould spray, and dry it. Then run the hottest empty wash the machine has with a machine cleaner or a cup of bicarbonate of soda, clean the detergent drawer and the filter out, and leave the door and the drawer open between washes so the drum dries. Use liquid detergent rather than powder at low temperatures and stop leaving wet washing in the drum. A seal that is black right through and slimy will not clean up: it is a cheap part and an easy swap.

The boll of the cotton plant, which is a ball of fluff around the seed: the fibres are picked, ginned out of the seed, combed straight and spun into thread. The plant wants heat and a long dry season, which is why so much of it grows in India, China and the southern United States.

The brackets go up first. Hold the shelf where you want it, mark the holes through the brackets with a pencil, take the shelf down, and fix the brackets to the wall with a fixing that suits it: a wall plug in brick or block, a screw into a stud, or a hollow-wall anchor in plasterboard with nothing behind it. Then screw the shelf to the brackets and check it with a spirit level along the shelf itself, not along one bracket.

The brain is a network of about 86 billion nerve cells that talk to each other through electrical and chemical signals. Different regions handle different jobs - movement, sight, language, emotion and memory - and the connections between them are what let you think, learn and remember; it runs on about 20 percent of the body's energy.

The brake fluid reservoir is the small pot near the back of the engine bay, marked with a circle in brackets; the level should sit between min and max. Do not open it to top up unless it is low, and if it is low there is a leak or worn pads, so get it checked. It gets changed every two years because it takes in water.

The brassicas are worth eating often and cost about 30 to 40 calories per 100g: broccoli has more vitamin C than an orange per 100g, and the whole family brings folate, vitamin K and fibre. Steam it for 4 or 5 minutes rather than boiling it to bits, since long cooking is what loses the vitamin C. There is nothing in them that detoxes anything - the reason to eat them is that they fill half a plate for very few calories.

The Blitz was the German bombing of British cities from September 1940 to May 1941, starting with 57 nights of raids on London. About 40,000 people were killed across the country, and the bombing never broke either the factories or the will to keep going.

The campaign for women's votes split into the peaceful suffragists and the militant suffragettes led by Emmeline Pankhurst. In Britain, women over 30 with property got the vote in 1918, and all women over 21 in 1928.

The can is sealed under pressure with a liquefied propellant above the paint or deodorant, and that liquid boils to keep the pressure steady as you use it. Pressing the nozzle lets the liquid out through a pinhole and it breaks into a mist; the can goes cold as it sprays and sputters at the end when the pressure finally drops.

The card through the door has a reference on it: put that into the courier's app and choose another day, a neighbour, or a local shop, usually free. Royal Mail keeps a parcel 18 days before sending it back and most couriers about a week, so book it within a couple of days. Collecting in person needs the card and photo ID with the address.

The card holds a chip and a tiny aerial, and the reader's radio field powers them, so there is no battery to run down. It answers with a one-time code instead of your real card number and the bank approves it online in under a second, which is why a number skimmed from a reader is hard to use again.

The cheapest way is usually a refurbished handset bought outright plus a SIM-only monthly plan: the same network for £8 to £15 a month instead of £30 to £50 bundled into a contract. Check the refurb is grade A or better with a 12-month warranty, and buy from the maker or a name you know rather than a marketplace seller.

The Boston Tea Party was a protest on 16 December 1773, when colonists dressed as Mohawks dumped 342 chests of taxed tea from three ships into Boston harbour. Britain closed the port in reply, and the two sides were at war within eighteen months.

The clock runs from the day you bought it, and a warranty has nothing to do with it: you can claim against the shop for up to six years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland and five in Scotland. Within 30 days you can reject it for a full refund, after that they get one repair or replacement, and for the first six months the shop has to prove the fault was not there when it sold it. Keep the receipt and put the claim in writing with photos.

The clock decides, not the look: two hours at room temperature is the limit, and one hour if the room is hot. Under that, box it and put it in the fridge and use it in the next day or two. Over it, bin anything with meat, fish, rice, dairy, eggs or a sauce, because the bugs that make you ill leave the taste and the smell alone and reheating does not undo it. Bread, cake, biscuits, jam and fruit are the exceptions and keep on the counter for days.

The clock is set with the two small buttons under the display, not with the dials: hold the one with the clock symbol until the hour flashes, tap the other to move it on, press the clock button for the minutes and then leave it alone for a few seconds to lock the time in. If it is flashing '0:00' after a power cut, the oven will not heat until it knows the time, which is why setting the clock is what puts the oven back on.

The cloud just means someone else's computer: your files are copied over the internet to a data centre and synced back to your devices. It is safer than only having them on one phone, but it is not a backup unless you keep a second copy somewhere else.

The clutch is the pedal that disconnects the engine from the gearbox, so you can change gear and pull away without the engine stalling: press it all the way down to change, then bring it up slowly as you add a little accelerator. Hold the car on the handbrake rather than on the clutch at a junction, because slipping it for long wears the plate out.

The coach is nearly always the cheapest and the train the fastest, and the price gap is all in how early you book: a coach booked a fortnight ahead is often a fiver, while a walk-up train fare on the day can be ten times that. Book a fixed-time train twelve weeks out for the cheap tiers, compare one change against a through train, and count the cost of getting to and from the stations before you decide.

The computer is waking the display, not the monitor doing it alone: a nudged mouse or a keypress, an overnight update, or a device on the same HDMI lead waking it through HDMI-CEC. Set the screen to sleep after five minutes (Settings > System > Power on Windows, System Settings > Displays on a Mac), switch off anything set to wake for the network, and in Command Prompt run powercfg -lastwake to see what did it.

The Bronze Age is when people learned to mix copper with tin to make bronze, from about 3,300 BC in the Middle East and about 2,200 BC in Britain. Bronze made better tools and weapons, trade grew to fetch the metals, and it ends around 800 BC in Britain, when ironworking took over.

The cord stump dries out and drops off on its own between about five days and a fortnight - clean and dry, water only, no cream or powder, and fold the nappy below it so air gets to it, and let it come away rather than pulling. A little bleeding at the very end is normal; a red, hot or smelly patch around the base, or pus, is a call to the midwife the same day. If it is still there at three weeks, mention it.

The council has to show photographs with the time, the place and the signs, so ask for the evidence and check whether the sign or the markings were clear. You have 28 days to appeal and usually 14 to pay at the reduced rate, and appealing inside that window keeps the discount. If they refuse, the free independent adjudicator is worth using: the Traffic Penalty Tribunal outside London, London Tribunals inside it.

The council's green bin is the cheapest route if you have one - many charge for the subscription and collect fortnightly - and the tip has a green waste skip. Grass, leaves and prunings can go in a compost bin at home too, but leave out cooked food, weeds in seed and anything diseased.

The cremation itself is a few hours, and it usually happens on the day of the funeral or within a day or two. The ashes are ready to collect in anything from a couple of days to a fortnight, and the crematorium rings you when they are. Ask the funeral director whether you are collecting them or the crematorium is scattering or burying them, and do not let anyone hurry the decision about what to do with them.

The crude benchmark the industry uses is a multiple of your salary: about your salary by 30, three times by 40, five times by 50 and seven times by the time you retire at 67, all in the pot rather than paid in. It is a rough guide, not a rule - someone with a final-salary scheme needs none of it and someone starting at 45 needs more - so the honest check is the free forecast on gov.uk for the state pension plus your scheme's own projection of what the pot turns into as an income.

The CPU is the chip that runs the instructions in every program; its speed is quoted in gigahertz and how many jobs it can do at once in cores. For everyday use - a browser, video calls, a spreadsheet - a mid-range chip from the last few years feels the same as a fast one, and more memory or an SSD makes a bigger difference.

The day is four set pieces, so rehearse them as set pieces: a group task where the group is watched not you (help the group finish, bring one quiet person in, do not talk over anyone), a short presentation (structure it out loud twice), a case study, and a competency interview in the same situation-task-action-result shape as any other interview. Do two timed practice numerical tests beforehand, and eat: people lose the group task to low blood sugar.

The deadline for a new PPI complaint was 29 August 2019, so a policy sold before then cannot be claimed on now, however the line is worded. Two things are still live: a policy you are still paying for can be cancelled today, and where the firm has gone bust the free Financial Services Compensation Scheme may still take it. Anyone texting that you are owed money and wants a fee up front is running a scam.

The decision has to be theirs, but you can make it much easier: pick a date together, say once what you have noticed and then leave it, and offer the nicotine patches or gum rather than a lecture. Keep the house and the car smoke-free, and do something else when the craving hits at the usual times. Expect two or three tries, so a slip is not a failure - just start again the next day.

The deductible, which in the UK is usually called the excess, is the first part of a claim you pay yourself: with a £250 excess on a £900 repair the insurer pays £650. A higher excess lowers the premium, so work out what you could actually find in a bad month before choosing one. Windscreen cover usually has a much smaller separate excess, often £75.

The dentist diagnoses and treats - check-ups, fillings, crowns, extractions; the hygienist cleans, scaling and polishing and checking your gums. Most practices book you with the hygienist every six months and the dentist for the check-up.

The diameter is the distance straight across a circle through its centre, and it is twice the radius. A circle 10 cm across has a radius of 5 cm and a circumference of about 31.4 cm, because circumference is pi times the diameter.

The doctor or coroner gives you the medical certificate; then you register the death at the local register office, within five days in England and Wales. Take that certificate, their birth certificate and NHS number. You leave with the death certificates for the bank and insurers, and a Tell Us Once code that tells the tax office, council and benefits at once. Scotland and Northern Ireland differ, so ask the register office.

The early signs are shaky, sweaty and hungry with a fast heart and tingling lips, and people often get irritable or muddled before they notice anything. Test if you have your meter; if you cannot, treat anyway - 15 to 20g of fast sugar, a small glass of juice or four glucose tablets, then retest in 15 minutes and repeat if it is still low. Follow it with a proper snack, or you will drop again.

The element has to heat through limescale before it reaches the water, so a badly scaled kettle can take twice as long - vinegar or citric acid brings it back to speed. Past that, a full kettle takes longer than a mugful, a 2kW kettle is about half the speed of a 3kW one, and very cold water is slower than water that has stood.

The empire had grown too big to govern from one place, so in 285 AD Diocletian split it into east and west, each with its own emperor; it divided for good in 395. The east, ruled from Constantinople, lasted another thousand years; the west fell in 476.

The equator is the imaginary line round the middle of the Earth, halfway between the poles at zero degrees latitude: day and night are about twelve hours each there all year, and the sun passes almost straight overhead.

The evidence says probably yes: fish have nerves and opioid receptors, and they learn to avoid a place where they were hurt. Scientists argued about it for years, and it is why handling rules for angling have tightened.

The fare is usually gone, but the tax and the airport charges come back: ask the airline in writing with the booking reference and most refund those even on a non-refundable ticket, often 30 to 60 pounds on a short-haul. Ring them before departure if you can, because many will move you to a later flight for a fee, and check whether your travel insurance covers the reason you could not go.

The filter is the usual culprit, behind the little kick plate at the bottom front: put a shallow bowl and a towel down, unscrew it slowly and pull out the coins and hair. Then check the drain hose behind the machine isn't kinked or pushed too far into the standpipe. If it still won't empty, the pump needs replacing, which is a cheap part and a half-hour job for an engineer.

The first sign is usually the periods changing - shorter or longer gaps, then skipped ones - with hot flushes, night sweats, broken sleep and a low mood for most women. The average age of the last period is 51, and a GP can tell from your symptoms without a blood test. Ask about HRT: it is the most effective help for flushes, sleep and mood, and safe for most women.

The first thing to ask for is a carer's assessment from your council: it is free, it is about you rather than the person you care for, and it can pay for someone to sit with them so you get a few hours back each week. Then tell your GP that you are caring - it goes on your notes, it counts for your own health, and it changes what they offer you. Ring Carers UK on 0808 808 7777 once, because they know the local schemes and the grants better than any website does, and ask your employer about flexible hours and unpaid carer's leave, which is now a day-one right. Book the break before you need it: a few hours a week arranged in advance is the difference between coping and going under, and taking it is not a failure.

The first three or four days after braces go on, and again for a day or two after each tighten, are the sore ones: take paracetamol or ibuprofen as the packet says and eat soft food for those days. Press a little orthodontic wax over any bracket or wire that rubs, and rinse with warm salt water if a cheek or lip is sore. Ring the orthodontist if a wire is digging in and you cannot ease it, if one tooth is much more painful than the rest, or if the pain is getting worse after a week rather than better.

The first three clients come from people who already know your work: a former employer or colleague, a friend who runs something, the local shop, a group you are already in. Pick one service you can name in a sentence, then tell twenty people you have started and what you charge - not a general announcement, one message each. Offer the first job small and priced so saying yes is easy, do it fast and well, and end every job by asking that client who else needs it. Two happy clients who recommend you beat any advert you could afford at this stage.

The first two to four weeks are the unsettled ones and they usually ease: go often and short rather than once for hours, keep to the same days so they can count on you, and make the room theirs with photos, their own blanket, a radio and a clock. Ask the staff what they have seen work for the person - the people who settle best are the ones whose family keeps turning up without making a fuss.

The first two to four weeks are the worst of it, and it eases after that even though nothing about it is linear: a bad day at week six is normal and not a relapse. What helps is people and ordinary structure - see someone today rather than when you feel up to it, keep eating and sleeping at the usual times, and get outside once a day. Keep the messages short and do not go looking for the reason at midnight.

The first week is the hardest and it does get easier: a craving peaks in about five minutes and the gaps between them stretch out after the third or fourth day. Expect a few days of being short-tempered and foggy, and a cough that brings up more than usual - the airways clearing is a good sign, not a relapse. The carbon monoxide is gone within a couple of days, breathing is easier in two to twelve weeks, and if a bad moment arrives, ride it out with water and a walk rather than testing your willpower.

The first £30,000 of a redundancy payment is tax free, and anything above that is taxed at your usual rate - so most people pay nothing on it at all. The £30,000 counts the whole package, not just the statutory part, and pay in lieu of notice and holiday pay are taxed as ordinary wages. If payroll takes tax off the whole thing, compare it with that figure and ask them to show you the working.

The five-second rule is not real: bacteria stick the moment food touches the floor, and it is the wetness that decides how much, not the seconds. A dry biscuit or a piece of toast is a small risk - brush it off and use your judgement - but anything damp, sticky or eaten with your hands should go in the bin, and anything dropped outside or in a bathroom always should. If it did go down, it is a wait-and-see, not a hospital trip: a healthy stomach usually deals with it.

The flu jab is one injection in the arm, best in October, and it is free on the NHS for anyone over 65, pregnant women, children from 2 up to 17 as a nasal spray, carers, and people with asthma, diabetes, heart, lung or kidney disease or a weakened immune system. It cannot give you flu; a sore arm for a day or two is the usual reaction. A pharmacy or the GP surgery books it.

The four-in-hand is the one to learn: put the tie round your neck with the wide end hanging about 30cm lower, cross it over the narrow end, take it up through the loop at your neck, then wrap it across the front and up through the loop again, and pull it down through the knot you just made. Draw it up snug and slide the knot where you want it. Wide end below the narrow, and the tip reaching your belt.

The fuse is chosen for the appliance, not the plug: 3A for a lamp, a radio or anything on a thin flex, 5A for a small appliance like a TV or a music system, and 13A for a kettle, heater, iron, toaster or anything that makes heat. If the right fuse blows again straight away, the appliance itself is faulty - stop changing fuses and have it looked at.

The garden in winter is mostly tidying and waiting: clear the dead stems but leave seed heads and any hollow stalks standing, because insects shelter in them and the birds eat the seeds. Mulch bare soil with compost or bark, but only once the ground is not frozen, and stay off wet or frozen grass because footprints kill the blades under them. Prune apples and pears and any shrub that flowers on this year's wood, clean and sharpen the tools, and wash out the greenhouse with a mild disinfectant before spring sowing. Pots are what the cold kills, so move them against a wall, raise them onto feet so the drainage hole does not sit in water, and give tender plants a layer of bubble wrap. Check the stored produce and the dahlias every couple of weeks for rot, and order seeds in January, because the quiet months are the only time the garden has nothing urgent in it.

The gas shut-off is the lever on the pipe beside the meter, usually in a box outside or under the stairs: a quarter turn so the lever sits across the pipe rather than along it turns the gas off. If you can smell gas, do not touch a switch, a light or a phone indoors - open the windows, get everyone out and ring the gas emergency line from outside: 0800 111 999 in England, Scotland and Wales, 0800 002 001 in Northern Ireland, 911 in the US. Only a Gas Safe engineer turns it back on.

The glycaemic index rates a food by how fast its carbohydrate raises blood sugar compared with pure glucose, from 0 to 100: a banana is about 50, white bread about 75, porridge oats about 55, lentils about 30. Low is 55 or under, and the trick is the company the carbohydrate keeps - fat, protein and fibre all slow it down, which is why a boiled potato beats a baked one and lentils barely move the number.

The government runs the country day to day - the prime minister, the cabinet and their departments - and parliament makes and checks the laws. If you want to know why, ask once, plainly; if there is no answer, let the silence be the answer and put your time into the people who turn up.

Treat it like a habit to break: mute their notifications, put the photos in a hidden album and fill the times you would normally text with something out of the house. It fades faster when you stop checking, and friends who knew you before help more than re-reading the last message.

Trim it in late August, straight after flowering: take the flower stalks off plus about 2.5cm of this year's leafy growth, and never cut into the bare brown wood, because it does not grow back. That keeps it dense and stops it going leggy, and leaving a little new growth on in autumn gives the plant something to shelter behind in winter. The other half of looking after it is the ground: full sun and sharp drainage, a gravelly or raised bed, because lavender rots in wet heavy soil in winter and that is the one thing that kills it. Water it for its first summer only - after that the rain is enough.
Try something with your hands: a new recipe, a jigsaw, or tidying one drawer.

Try the other size of ear tip first: most earbuds come with three, most people are wearing one size too big, and the seal, not the loudness, is what keeps them in. Twist them in and back a little so the tip points into the ear canal rather than straight at it, and use the one earbud with the hook over the top of the ear when you are moving about. On a wired pair with buds that drop out, the small silicone wings or a foam tip cost a few pounds and hold far better. If it is the headband that aches, slide the cups so the band sits further back and the pads sit around the ear rather than pressing on it, and take them off for ten minutes every hour: a headache behind the ears is the clamp, not the volume.

Try the smallest real version first: an evening course, one freelance job, or a sideways move inside your current employer. Talk to three people doing the job now and ask what the bad days are like, not the good ones. Most successful switches are 18 months of steady part-time effort, not a leap.

Try the cable and plug you know work on something else, then clean the port out with a wooden toothpick - a ball of pocket fluff is the usual cause.
